events.text: A letter comes for {b3_clan}, in a hand nobody knows, with every title right and in the right order. Somebody has been keeping a file on you. {b3_elder} reads it over your shoulder and says nothing, in the manner of a person who has just won an argument fifty years old.

choices.text: Answer it in full

effects.log: You answer in full, and the reply comes back inside the month, warmer, with a request in the last line.

choices.text: Let {b3_elder} answer

effects.log: {b3_elder} writes four lines and enjoys every one of them. The house is spoken of a little more carefully after that.

events.text: The cooks of other houses now send over their best recipes unasked, which is how you learn the neighbours have started to watch what {b3_clan} eats. {b3_peer} is delighted. {b3_elder} says an honest house is never fashionable for long, and goes back to the ledger.

choices.text: Hold a dinner to match the talk

effects.log: The dinner is a small triumph and a large bill. Three houses ask to be seated nearer, and one of them means it.

choices.text: Eat what you always ate

effects.log: You eat what you always ate. It is noted, in the quiet way of such notes, that the house does not perform.

events.text: A child of another house is sent to be fostered with {b3_clan} for a year, which is a thing only done to a house one admires or fears. The child is polite, observant and carries a notebook. {b3_peer} is certain the notebook is a spy. {b3_elder} says every notebook is.

choices.text: Let the child read anything

effects.log: The child reads everything and goes home with a very good opinion of you, which will be repeated for two hundred years at the wrong tables.

choices.text: Keep the ledgers locked

effects.log: The ledgers stay locked. The notebook finds what it finds without them, and the child is kind about it on leaving.

events.text: Your seat in the Cloud Tablet hall is moved, and nobody tells you. You find out when you go in and the chair has been set a step nearer the door of honour. It was {b3_elder} who did it, at night, with a stool and a great deal of grunting, because the house has risen and the old arrangement lied.

choices.text: Thank {b3_elder} in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {b3_elder} aloud. The old one goes red to the ears and says it was only the stool.

choices.text: Sit in the new place and say nothing

effects.log: You sit in it as if you had always sat there. The house relaxes, and so, slightly, do you.

events.text: Strangers now ask which branch of {b3_clan} you are. There are no branches. There is you, and the people you have gathered, and a good deal of luck. But the question has an answer people want, and a very ambitious cousin of a faraway family says he is willing to supply one for a fee.

choices.text: Refuse, and say the house has one root

effects.log: You say the house has one root and is proud of it. It becomes a saying within the year, and the faraway cousin writes a bitter letter.

choices.text: Let the branches be invented, quietly

effects.log: The branches are invented in the proper handwriting. The house gains a past, and loses something you cannot name.

events.text: The dead of {b3_clan} have never had a proper wall. {b3_elder} says it plainly: the cloud tablets were put up by someone who thought the house would last a decade. Now it has lasted a century and the names crowd each other. A mason of rank offers to build something fitting, and it will take years.

choices.text: Build the wall, and carve every name

effects.log: The wall goes up over eleven years, name by name, and the masons grow fond of the house. It is spoken of for its dead.

choices.text: Keep the old ones; carve only the new

effects.log: The old tablets stay crooked and honest. The house keeps its humility, and loses a little polish in the eyes of visitors.

events.text: A rival house sends a gift, a very fine one, on the day {b3_clan} is first named in their company. It is a gift that cannot be refused without insult or accepted without owing. {b3_peer} holds it up to the light and says it has the weight of a hook.

choices.text: Return it with a better gift

effects.log: You return it with a gift that is a shade better. The rival house stops sending things, and starts sending nods.

choices.text: Accept it and owe it gladly

effects.log: You accept and owe it, and the rival house is delighted, for an owed house is a held one. It will be used, sometime.

events.text: In the third quiet hour a petitioner is found at the gate of {b3_clan}, asking to be taken in as a servant, not a guest. A servant of a house that rises is a servant of status. The petitioner is the last of a ruined line, still carrying a tablet no bigger than a hand.

choices.text: Take the tablet in, and the petitioner with it

effects.log: The tablet is set in the Cloud Tablet hall beside your own. The petitioner serves for forty years and never once asks for more than the tablet's place.

choices.text: Give them a post at a neighbour house

effects.log: You find them a good post at a neighbour house, and a letter. They go, and the neighbour house is in your debt.

events.text: {b3_clan} was always the house that arrived late and sat low. Now a visitor of great name asks, quite innocently, whether {b3_clan} has always been so old. {b3_elder} looks at you. It has not. But old is what the visitor has decided the house is, and the visitor is repeating it to everyone.

choices.text: Say it has always been so

effects.log: You say so. The word old settles on the house like a good coat, and {b3_elder} will not meet your eye for a week.

choices.text: Say it is new, and means to be old

effects.log: You say it is new and means to be old. The visitor laughs and repeats that instead, and it is better than the lie.

events.text: A young one of your blood, flush with the house's new importance, has taken to being carried about on a skiff with the crest painted on the side. {b3_elder} has stopped speaking to the young one. {b3_peer} thinks it is wonderful. The house has a risen name and no manners to go with it yet.

choices.text: Take the young one on a long, humble errand

effects.log: The errand is long and humble, and the young one comes back quieter and, quietly, better. The crest is painted over by choice.

choices.text: Let the young one enjoy it

effects.log: The young one enjoys it for a season, and some visitor is amused in a way that costs you a little, later.

events.text: A chronicler of the neighbouring houses arrives to write {b3_clan} into the great record, and is polite in the particular way of someone being paid. The first question is about your founding. The second is about your enemies. The chronicler admits the second is the one the record is read for.

choices.text: Tell the plain founding and name your enemies fairly

effects.log: You tell it plainly and name your enemies fairly. The chronicler looks, for the first time, a little ashamed of the fee.

choices.text: Tell a handsome founding

effects.log: The founding is handsome and mostly true. It goes into the record, and in a century will be fully true.

events.text: The hearth-fires of {b3_clan} are counted in the house records, and for the first time the count is high enough to be quoted. {b3_peer} quotes it at dinner. {b3_elder} notes, mildly, that every fire counted is a mouth to feed and a grudge to keep, and that the quote will be remembered by people less friendly.

choices.text: Open the doors of the hall to the poorer kin

effects.log: You open the hall to the poorer kin that week. The house is crowded and quarrelsome and, by spring, undeniably larger in heart.

choices.text: Close ranks and keep the count quiet

effects.log: You close ranks. The count is not quoted again, and the house is the quieter for it.

events.text: A rank-and-file steward of the older houses, one who has refused every visit of yours for years, leaves a single scroll on your threshold with no name. It is a copy of the register of the house you now outrank. The scroll is not an insult and is not a gift. It is a statement that the older house has stopped pretending.

choices.text: Return the scroll with a seat of honour for its house

effects.log: You send it back with an offer of the seat of honour. The older house will never forgive you for making it so easy, and never forget it.

choices.text: Keep the scroll, and read the register

effects.log: You read the register for a week. It is humbling and useful, and the older house is a little relieved to be understood.

events.text: On the night the new rank is read out, no one in the house can sleep. {b3_elder} sits up by the mist door, and {b3_peer} paces, and you find yourself counting the tiles of the cloud court for the third time. Rising turns out to feel mostly like being watched by people who are not there yet.

choices.text: Go and sit with {b3_elder}

effects.log: You sit with {b3_elder} until grey light. Neither of you says a thing worth recording. It is the best part of the whole honour.

choices.text: Go out and walk the boundary alone

effects.log: You walk the boundary alone, and it is smaller than your fear and larger than you thought. Dawn finds you home.

events.text: Two houses that have never agreed on anything agree on one point: that {b3_clan} has risen too fast. They say it in separate letters on the same day, in near-identical phrasing, and then both ask for a favour. {b3_peer} laughs until it hurts. {b3_elder} points out that the favour is the same favour.

choices.text: Grant the favour to both, and let them find out

effects.log: You grant it to both. They find out in a season, and each one blames the other, which is a better result than thanks.

choices.text: Grant it to neither

effects.log: You grant it to neither. They are, for the first time in their histories, united in resentment, which you may regret.

events.text: {b3_peer} has been telling the younger ones that the jade seal was meant to pass by blood and not by choice, and that you, whatever else, were chosen. It is an old argument and it is not entirely wrong. The younger ones are listening.

choices.text: Call {b3_peer} in and ask what they want

effects.log: {b3_peer} wants to be asked, it turns out, and a post in the east wing. The post is given, and the talk quietens. It is cheap.

choices.text: Say it in the open: the seal was chosen, and why

effects.log: You say it in the open, with reasons. Some are persuaded, and {b3_peer} is not, and is now openly an opponent.

events.text: The ledger of {b3_clan} is short by a quantity that would be quite impossible to explain as a mistake. {b3_elder} found it, and has come to you in a state of cold grief, because there are only four people who touch the ledger, and one of them is {b3_elder}.

choices.text: Hold a quiet reckoning with the four

effects.log: The reckoning is quiet and miserable. The shortfall turns out to be a kindness to a failing sibling, paid for by the clerk, who has been starving to hide it.

choices.text: Order the ledger rewritten and move on

effects.log: You rewrite the ledger, and move on. The shortfall continues, now quietly, for years.

events.text: An old rule of the house says that the Cloud Tablet hall must be swept by the blood, never by servants, once in each season. The house now numbers hundreds. The rule is kept by fewer each year. {b3_elder} has taken to doing it alone and reproachfully, at dawn, where everyone can hear the broom.

choices.text: Take up a broom yourself

effects.log: You take up a broom. By the third dawn there are eleven of you, mostly ashamed, and the hall has never been cleaner.

choices.text: Change the rule to a rota of duties

effects.log: You change the rule into a rota. It is fair, and works, and {b3_elder} says nothing for a month in a tone that rings.

events.text: A betrothal made two generations ago by an ancestor of {b3_clan} is called in by the other house, at the worst possible time. The match is not wanted by anyone living on either side. The other house wants it for the land that comes with it. It has the deed, and a great-uncle's signature.

choices.text: Honour it, and let the young ones choose their peace within it

effects.log: You honour it, and make the match a quiet friendship instead of a marriage. Neither side is wholly satisfied, which suggests it was fair.

choices.text: Contest the deed on a technicality

effects.log: You contest it on a technicality that the other house's own scribe confirms. The land stays, and the grudge begins.

choices.text: Persuade the other house to forget it

ok.log: You persuade the other house, over a long supper, that the ancestors would have laughed. They laugh. The deed is burned.

fail.log: The other house hears you out with great courtesy, and keeps the deed. The match lies on the house like a stone.

events.text: {b3_clan} and its nearest neighbour have shared a boundary stream for ages, and the neighbour has begun to dam it. It is a very small dam. It is also the principle. {b3_peer} wants to unmake it by night. {b3_elder} wants to send a delegation with a gift of fish.

choices.text: Send {b3_elder} with the fish

effects.log: {b3_elder} goes with the fish and comes back with a promise of a sluice. It is a diplomatic victory that no one will ever remember.

choices.text: Let {b3_peer} unmake the dam by night

effects.log: The dam is gone by morning, and the neighbour house knows exactly who. The quarrel turns hot, and you are, a little, proud.

choices.text: Build a second, better dam together

effects.log: You propose a shared dam, and it is built with two houses' labour, resentfully, and is a very good dam.

events.text: A cousin of {b3_clan} has been caught writing letters to another house, signed with the name of the house's own steward. It was not treason: it was a love letter, a very bad one, to the heir of the other house. The household is quite divided between horror and a certain delight.

choices.text: Let it stand, and see where the letters go

effects.log: You let it stand. The cousin and the heir elope, eventually, in a cart, and the two houses are bound by a scandal that is almost a treaty.

choices.text: Break it off, gently, for both houses

effects.log: You break it off, gently, with a carefully worded note. Both parties are heartbroken for a decade, and the two houses are polite.

events.text: The house of the isle cannot agree on a day for the Moon Feast. {b3_peer} says the old day, the dawn of the first month. {b3_elder} says the new, which suits the guests. Neither will bend, and the cooks have laid down their knives.

choices.text: Keep the old day, and hold the new as a second feast

effects.log: Two feasts it is, and the house eats well for it, and nobody can complain. The cooks, however, remember.

choices.text: Choose the new day and say so

effects.log: You choose the new day. {b3_peer} sits at the far end like a thundercloud, and the guests are delighted.

events.text: A great aunt of {b3_clan} has declared that she will leave her property, which is considerable, to whichever of the younger blood is the first to give her a great-grandchild. The younger blood have begun to eye one another. {b3_peer} is making calculations aloud.

choices.text: Forbid the contest as unseemly

effects.log: You forbid it. The great aunt is furious and charmed, and changes the will to leave it to the house as a whole.

choices.text: Let it go on, and watch

effects.log: You let it go on. It is a comedy for a season and a mild disgrace after, and a very pretty child comes out of it.

events.text: A branch of the house has been cut off for a hundred years by an act of a long-dead head, for a crime nobody can now name. A descendant of that branch appears at the gate, with the proper crest, hat in hand. {b3_elder} says the quarrel is older than all the quarrellers.

choices.text: Lift the ban and seat them

effects.log: You lift the ban and seat the descendant low at the table. {b3_elder} is angry for an hour, and then weeps, and the house is the larger.

choices.text: Hear their case, but keep the ban

effects.log: You hear the case, and keep the ban, courteously, and the descendant goes away with the face of someone who has expected exactly this.

events.text: {b3_elder}, keeper of the house's memory, has begun to forget. It is small at first: a name, a date, and then the way to the Cloud Tablet hall. The house is quietly, desperately, writing down everything the old one still knows before it is gone. {b3_peer} suggests a successor.

choices.text: Sit with {b3_elder} and write it down yourself

effects.log: You sit with {b3_elder} for a year of afternoons. The record that results is the finest the house possesses, and the old one dies knowing it was kept.

choices.text: Appoint {b3_peer} as keeper at once

effects.log: {b3_peer} takes the post with surprising gravity, and is a better keeper than anyone feared. {b3_elder} is hurt and grateful.

events.text: Two of your younger kin quarrelled at a feast, and one struck the other. It is an old, bad thing in {b3_clan}: a blow in the Cloud Tablet hall is a blow to all. The striker is now hiding in the cloud larder, and the struck one is dignified and furious in the best room.

choices.text: Make the striker kneel before the whole house

effects.log: The striker kneels in front of the whole house, shaking. It is awful, and effective, and nobody strikes anyone else for forty years.

choices.text: Settle it privately between the two

effects.log: You settle it privately, over a night and a pot of tea. They are friends by morning, in the way the young can be.

events.text: A merchant house has offered to buy {b3_clan}'s old orchard, at a price that would cure a hundred small embarrassments. The orchard is where the first of the house is buried. {b3_peer} says a tree is a tree. {b3_elder} says that the first of the house would say otherwise, and would say it in the market.

choices.text: Refuse, and plant a new tree as thanks

effects.log: You refuse, and plant a young tree in the offer's honour. The merchant house, half-amused, becomes a friend.

choices.text: Sell all but the grave's ground

effects.log: You sell everything but the grave's ground. The money is spent well, and the orchard is spoken of as a loss, now and again, for a hundred years.

events.text: A house of lesser rank in the district has quietly stopped bowing to {b3_clan} at the turn of the road. It is not rebellion. It is a mild, deliberate tilt of the head, one finger less than correct. The whole lane is watching. {b3_peer} wants satisfaction. {b3_elder} wants to count the fingers.

choices.text: Return the bow, exactly as given

effects.log: You return the tilt, precisely, one finger less. The lane holds its breath, and then the other house laughs and bows properly.

choices.text: Call at their gate with a gift of tea

effects.log: You call with tea. It is such perfect manners that the lesser house is shamed into a year of excellent behaviour.

events.text: The house physician has told you, privately, that {b3_elder} is in the habit of taking a small portion from the house stores and giving it to a family beyond the wall, without a word to anyone. The family is very poor and very proud. It has been going on for twenty years.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let it go on

effects.log: You say nothing, and a little of the stores goes on leaving at dusk. When {b3_elder} dies the family comes to the gate with a wreath, and the house hears the whole story.

choices.text: Make it an open, official kindness

effects.log: You make it a house custom, with a ledger. It is more help and much less grace, and {b3_elder} is silent for a week.

events.text: A tutor engaged for the younger blood of {b3_clan} teaches with great passion and, it turns out, entirely the wrong history of the house, in which the founder was a hero in every particular. The young repeat it proudly. {b3_elder} has been seen weeping into a sleeve.

choices.text: Quietly correct the tutor, and give them the true story

effects.log: You give the tutor the true story and the sources, and in a year it is the better lesson. The founder, with flaws, is now loved.

choices.text: Let the myth stand; they are young

effects.log: You let it stand. The young are proud, and loyal, and a little foolish, which is perhaps what a house needs.

events.text: The east wing and the west wing of {b3_clan} have not spoken for a decade over the matter of who shall hold the jade seal in your absence. Each now has a champion. {b3_peer} leads the east, loudly. The west has gone silent, which {b3_elder} says is far more dangerous.

choices.text: Divide the seal's duties among both wings

effects.log: You divide the duties, and the wings must work together or fail. They fail, then work, then become, grudgingly, one house again.

choices.text: Name a third party to hold it

effects.log: You name an outsider's old friend as holder. Both wings are insulted equally, which is, you hope, a kind of fairness.

events.text: A pair of bold young ones of {b3_clan} have been climbing out at night to attend the debates of another house, and returning with ideas. The ideas are good. They are also unlicensed, and the head of the other house has sent a stiff note asking whether {b3_clan} cannot keep its blood at home.

choices.text: Let them go, and send a gracious reply

effects.log: You write a gracious reply, and the young ones keep going, quietly sponsored. The other house, in time, is proud of the visitors.

choices.text: Forbid it, and invite the debate here

effects.log: You forbid it and host the debates yourself. It is a great trouble, and the house is the better for the company.

events.text: There is a tradition in {b3_clan} that each head plants one tree, and each tree is a measure of its head. {b3_peer} points out, in the tone of someone discovering a weapon, that yours has not yet been planted. {b3_elder} is holding a very expensive sapling and looking at the sky.

choices.text: Plant it at once, in the worst corner

effects.log: You plant it in the worst corner of the yard, where nothing grows. It is a stubborn tree, and in a century will be the pride of the house.

choices.text: Plant it where the young will climb it

effects.log: You plant it in the middle of the yard, to be climbed. It is knocked half down in three years, and loved, and well.

events.text: The house's oldest servant, who has served three heads, has asked to be buried in the family ground. There is no precedent. There is, however, no rule against it, and {b3_peer} says that is exactly why it must not be done. {b3_elder} says that is exactly why it must.

choices.text: Grant it, with full rites

effects.log: You grant it with full rites. The house stands a long time in the rain at the burying, and the servant's name is carved by the founder's.

choices.text: Grant it, in a plain grave beside the wall

effects.log: You grant a plain grave beside the wall. It is what the servant would have chosen, and {b3_elder} says so.

events.text: A splendid heirloom of {b3_clan}, a thing the whole house reveres, has been found to be a clever copy. The real one was sold by an ancestor to pay a debt, and the copy made in shame. Only the old books say so. {b3_elder} found the line, and now will not eat.

choices.text: Tell the house the whole truth

effects.log: You tell the house. There is a week of shock and then, oddly, great tenderness for the ancestor who made a fake for love of his name.

choices.text: Keep the secret, and honour the copy

effects.log: You keep the secret. The copy is revered as ever, and you and {b3_elder} share a look across the hall at every feast.

events.text: A house of the old quarter has declared a blood-price for an insult of ages past: a word said in a corridor six hundred years ago, preserved in their annals. The sum asked is not ruinous. It is the principle. They have sent their steward, who looks dismayed to be here.

choices.text: Pay it with a short, grave letter

effects.log: You pay it, with a letter of exactly one line of regret. The steward weeps with relief, and the old house is reconciled to a degree.

choices.text: Find the word in your own annals and answer in kind

effects.log: You find the same word, said in the other direction, in your annals, and send the bill back. The old house, sputtering, withdraws.

events.text: {b3_peer} has got engaged, without consulting anyone, to a person of whom the house knows nothing and the neighbourhood far too much. The person is charming, indebted, and has a past. {b3_elder} has quietly done a little research and does not look well.

choices.text: Hold a supper for the two, and judge for yourself

effects.log: The supper is long. The person, it turns out, is better than the rumours, and also heavily in debt, and {b3_peer} learns to be careful with money in a year.

choices.text: Forbid the match

effects.log: You forbid the match. {b3_peer} sulks for years, is ultimately saved a good deal of grief, and never thanks you.

events.text: A fire in the north store of {b3_clan} burned a season's spirit stones and the records with it. No one was hurt. Everyone is looking at each other and at the lamp that was left burning. {b3_elder} says nothing; {b3_peer} says it was not them, three times, in a rising voice.

choices.text: Name the loss as the house's and not anyone's

effects.log: You say the house owes the loss, and the house takes it up, and no one is made to pay. {b3_peer} weeps in the hall, with relief, and tells everyone.

choices.text: Find the lamp-tender and put it right quietly

effects.log: You find the tender, a frightened child, and put it right quietly. The child works for the house for sixty years afterwards, with a certain devotion.

events.text: It is the year of the house's great reunion. Relatives have come from far, some not seen in decades. One of them, a stranger to everyone, is introduced by {b3_peer} as an uncle. {b3_elder}, who knows the genealogy cold, whispers that there is no such uncle.

choices.text: Say nothing, and watch what the stranger wants

effects.log: You watch. The stranger wants only to belong, and has invented an uncle's part out of loneliness. You let it be, and the house gains a relative.

choices.text: Question the stranger gently in private

effects.log: You ask in private. The stranger confesses, and weeps, and is taken in anyway, which is the finest thing the house does that year.

events.text: The younger generation of {b3_clan} has asked for a say in how the house is run. They call it a council, and have drawn up rules, some quite sensible. {b3_elder} treats the matter as a flood. {b3_peer} has agreed to chair it, and has already ordered cushions.

choices.text: Grant the council a real, small voice

effects.log: You grant the council the care of the festivals and the young. It is real and small, and it is a surprisingly good thing, and the old are shocked.

choices.text: Receive the rules with thanks and file them

effects.log: You receive the rules with thanks and file them. The young feel handled, which they are, and the house goes on much as it was.

events.text: A great storm tore the tiled roof of jade shingle of the old wing, and the damage is plain, expensive and rather beautiful: the old beams show through, and the eaves are open to the sky. {b3_peer} wants to rebuild at once. {b3_elder} wants it left open for a season, as a lesson.

choices.text: Leave it open for a season

effects.log: The old wing stands open to the sky for a season. The house learns something about itself, and a swallow nests in a beam.

choices.text: Rebuild at once

effects.log: You rebuild at once, handsomely, and the old wing is better than before. {b3_elder} is a little sorry, and says nothing.

events.text: There is a recipe the women of {b3_clan} have kept for generations, in a family of cooks, and it is said that no outsider has ever tasted it. A rival house has just served it at a feast. The cook is in tears. {b3_peer} suspects a servant. {b3_elder} suspects a daughter-in-law.

choices.text: Find out quietly, and forgive

effects.log: You find out: it was a young cook who had left on bad terms. You forgive, and invite them back, and the recipe is, from then on, shared.

choices.text: Make the rival house pay for the recipe

effects.log: You make the rival house pay, in a long letter, in coin that you can name. It stops, and the cook is vindicated.

events.text: A lawsuit between two branches of the house, over a boundary hedge, has gone on since before {b3_elder} was born. It has been inherited like a name. Both sides now come to you at once, with documents, and both look slightly relieved at the thought that someone might end it.

choices.text: Walk the hedge with both sides and decide on the spot

effects.log: You walk the hedge with both sides, and decide by the oldest oak. Both are cross, and both are free, and the hedge is trimmed that evening.

choices.text: Refuse to hear it; they are one house

effects.log: You refuse to hear it. It takes a season of sulking, and then one branch quietly clips the other's side of the hedge.

events.text: The young of {b3_clan} want to leave the isle for a season, and see the others: the Eight Houses, the world below, anything. {b3_elder} says no young one of the blood has ever left without a ship of the house. The young say that is exactly why they have never learned to steer.

choices.text: Let them go in pairs, with a modest sum

effects.log: They go in pairs, with a modest sum. Some come back wiser, some not at all, and the house has a dozen new friends and a few new enemies.

choices.text: Send an escort and a tutor with each

effects.log: They go with escorts and tutors, and see less than they hoped, and come back safe. The house exhales.

events.text: An old family compact, signed by the founders of two houses, says that each shall come to the other's aid in want, without question. The other house is now in want. It is a house you dislike. {b3_peer} points out that the compact is old and unclear and perhaps expired. {b3_elder} says the compact was never about liking.

choices.text: Honour it fully

effects.log: You honour it fully, grudgingly, with grain and goodwill. The other house survives, and a lifetime of grudges is turned to a certain reluctant gratitude.

choices.text: Honour it to the letter, and no further

effects.log: You honour it to the letter. The other house is saved, and is not grateful, and remembers it.

events.text: {b3_clan} has a name for being good at weddings: the best food, the best music, the best quarrels in the kitchen. A great house asks, as a kindness, if it may borrow the cooks for its own. {b3_peer} says it is flattery. {b3_elder} says it is flattery and also a favour, and you may not decline both.

choices.text: Lend the cooks, and attend the wedding

effects.log: You lend the cooks, and attend. It is the finest wedding of the decade, and the house is asked to a good many more.

choices.text: Lend the recipes but keep the cooks

effects.log: You lend the recipes. The great house's cooks ruin them lovingly, and the whole district talks about it, kindly.

events.text: A dead head of the house left a sealed chest, to be opened at a bad time, by a head in trouble. {b3_elder} says this is that time. {b3_peer} says it is not, and the chest should wait for worse. Everyone has a theory about the contents. No one admits to having a theory.

choices.text: Open it now

effects.log: You open it. It holds a short letter, a pressed leaf, and the instruction: do not trouble yourself so much. {b3_elder} laughs until crying.

choices.text: Keep it sealed, for worse

effects.log: You keep it sealed. Knowing it is there is, oddly, a comfort, and you do not open it for a long time.

events.text: There is a stair in the house that no one uses, and no one will say why. The young have found that it leads to a small room with a window, and a tablet, face to the wall. {b3_peer} has turned it round. It is the name of a head who was struck from the record.

choices.text: Restore the name to the register

effects.log: You restore the name. The reasons for its striking were small and old, and the house feels, strangely, whole.

choices.text: Turn the tablet back to the wall, and keep the room

effects.log: You turn it back, and leave the room tidy and the window open. You will not say why, but {b3_elder} nods once.

events.text: A messenger of another house has come to say that its head has died, and the whole house, in a strange gesture, wants {b3_clan} to name the successor. It is a trap or a trust, and the messenger himself does not know which. {b3_peer} says take the trust. {b3_elder} says take the trap.

choices.text: Decline to name, and send an observer to the funeral

effects.log: You decline, with all courtesy, and send an observer. The other house makes its own choice, and remembers that you had the sense not to meddle.

choices.text: Name the successor, and be answerable

effects.log: You name one. It is a heavy gift: the new head is your creature for life, whether either of you wishes it.

events.text: The young ones of {b3_clan} have started a quarrel with the young ones of the house over the wall: a game, a stolen ball, a broken window. It has become a war of pranks. {b3_elder} is secretly enjoying it. {b3_peer} is running the intelligence.

choices.text: Call a truce with a joint festival

effects.log: You call a truce and a joint festival, and the two houses are for a time almost unbearable with cheer. The pranks go on, a little more affectionately.

choices.text: Let it run, within bounds

effects.log: You let it run within bounds. A season of pranks, and no real harm, and both houses grow up a little.

events.text: A strong bad winter has left half the house sick, and the remaining half more cross than anyone has seen. {b3_elder} has taken over the kitchens. {b3_peer} has taken over the infirmary. Both have taken over you, in the sense of arguing about whether you should sleep.

choices.text: Sleep, as ordered

effects.log: You sleep, and they both look after the house in different, quarrelling, brilliant ways. When you wake the worst is over and the house has learned to run without you.

choices.text: Work through it at the bedsides

effects.log: You work through, and are exhausted, and the house loves you for it for a long time.

events.text: An outsider who has taught the younger blood for years has been caught at some small dishonesty, a matter of a borrowed book. {b3_peer} wants them dismissed. The students, to a one, have lined up outside the study door. {b3_elder} has gone for a walk.

choices.text: Let the tutor stay, with a rueful apology

effects.log: You let the tutor stay. The apology is real, and the students are fiercely loyal, and the house acquires, in a stroke, a man who will never again take anything.

choices.text: Dismiss them, with a good reference

effects.log: You dismiss them with a very good reference. The students are bitter, and the tutor is grateful, and the house is quieter.

events.text: The bell of the house, which has called its blood to meals for as long as anyone knows, has cracked. {b3_peer} wants it recast. {b3_elder} says the crack gives it its voice, and that the founder's voice was cracked too.

choices.text: Keep the cracked bell, and ring it as it is

effects.log: You keep it. The sound is strange and dear, and the visitors say it is a bell with a story, which it is.

choices.text: Recast it, and keep the old metal in the new

effects.log: You recast it with the old metal in the new. It rings clear, and when it rings {b3_elder} touches the wall.

events.text: Two aunts of {b3_clan} have not spoken for thirty years, over a dress. Both are dying, slowly, in rooms on opposite sides of the cloud court. Every maid in the house has become a diplomat. {b3_elder} says you could end it in an afternoon. {b3_peer} says you will regret it.

choices.text: Carry a message from one aunt to the other

effects.log: You carry the first message across the yard. The reply is short and furious and, at its end, three words of tenderness. You carry them back.

choices.text: Leave them to it; it is theirs

effects.log: You leave them to it. They die within a month of each other, still not speaking, and are buried side by side, which is its own sort of end.

events.text: A new apprentice arrives for the house archivist, and in the first week finds an entire missing generation, a family of the blood who were never recorded, living in a hamlet three days off, quite unaware. {b3_peer} says it is forgery. {b3_elder} says no one could invent such a mess.

choices.text: Send a delegation to bring them home

effects.log: The delegation finds them. They are delighted and suspicious, in equal measure, and when they come to the house they bring bread and a tablet of their own.

choices.text: Send gifts, and leave them to decide

effects.log: You send gifts and a letter. They answer in an odd, careful hand, and are, by degrees, kin again.

events.text: The house boats of {b3_clan}, six of them, are the pride of the whole the isle, and the oldest is declared unsafe. {b3_elder} says that she carried the founder's wife. {b3_peer} says that is why she must be burned with honour. The shipwright is waiting with a quiet, professional smile.

choices.text: Refit her, at great expense

effects.log: You refit her. She floats like a swan, carries the young out to the festivals, and the shipwright is, for the rest of his life, very proud.

choices.text: Burn her with honour, on the water

effects.log: You burn her on the water at dusk. The whole house watches, and no one speaks, and the glow stays for an hour.

events.text: The cat of {b3_clan}, a venerable and malevolent creature, has taken up residence on the head's chair and refuses to be moved. The house considers it a sign. {b3_elder} says the cat has an excellent sense of seniority. {b3_peer} says the cat has no sense at all.

choices.text: Sit elsewhere, and let the cat reign

effects.log: You sit elsewhere. The cat reigns for six years, and the house is calmer in its presence, and every visitor leaves a small offering.

choices.text: Lift the cat down, firmly and kindly

effects.log: You lift the cat down. It sulks for a week and then takes the chair of the steward, who is delighted.

events.text: A young one of the blood, a prodigy at the house arts, has asked to leave {b3_clan} and study with its rival, because the rival has a master who is better. It is true. The master is better. The young one stands in the study with a bag, shaking, and has clearly rehearsed.

choices.text: Let the prodigy go, with the house's blessing

effects.log: You give your blessing, and a letter. The prodigy returns twenty years later greater than either house, and says whose name taught the first lesson.

choices.text: Ask the prodigy to stay one more year

effects.log: You ask for one more year, and use it to draw the master's lessons here by gift and letter. The prodigy stays, and is wiser, and a little hurt.

events.text: An old servant of {b3_clan} has been found, after fifty years, to be quietly writing a record of the house from the servants' side. It is plain, accurate, and unflattering to nearly everyone. It also mentions you, kindly. {b3_peer} wants it burned. {b3_elder} wants it copied.

choices.text: Copy it, and keep both in the archive

effects.log: You copy it. The servant's record sits beside the head's record for the next thousand years and corrects it in a hundred places.

choices.text: Ask the servant to keep writing, and read it each year

effects.log: You read it each year. It is a very good check on the head, and a humbling one.

events.text: The house wine-store of {b3_clan} has produced, by accident, something extraordinary: a vintage no one can reproduce. It is guarded by the butler like a child. Two other houses have already offered fortunes. {b3_peer} says sell. {b3_elder} says serve it only at funerals and weddings.

choices.text: Serve it only at funerals and weddings

effects.log: You serve it only then. The wine becomes the house's legend, and a funeral at {b3_clan} is spoken of for its dignity.

choices.text: Sell a measure, and hold the rest

effects.log: You sell one measure for a great sum, and hold the rest. The two houses are satisfied, and the butler grieves aloud.

events.text: The children of {b3_clan} have started a game in which the founder is a dragon and each head a different, very rude kind of animal. You are a goose. {b3_peer} overheard and was not amused. {b3_elder} says you ought to be pleased: only the beloved are made into animals.

choices.text: Join the game as the goose

effects.log: You join as the goose, with great seriousness. The children are in ecstasy, and the story of the goose head is told in the house for centuries.

choices.text: Pretend not to know

effects.log: You pretend not to know. You are, on the stair, often followed by a quiet honking, and you do not turn round.

events.text: A traveller of great learning is staying at {b3_clan}, and has offered to correct the house's account of its founding, which he says is wrong in four places. He is right in three. {b3_peer} is incandescent. {b3_elder} has taken notes with trembling hands.

choices.text: Correct the account in public, and thank him

effects.log: You correct it in public, with thanks. The house is humbled, and the learned traveller is, ever after, its friend.

choices.text: Thank him privately, and leave the account

effects.log: You thank him privately and leave the account. It is a small cowardice, and it holds the house together for a while.

events.text: The house register and the house gossip disagree about who was at the great quarrel of the last century. The register is clean. The gossip names everyone. A descendant of the one the gossip names has come to demand the register be amended. {b3_elder} has gone pale.

choices.text: Amend the register honestly, and apologise for the delay

effects.log: You amend it honestly. The descendant takes it with a long silence and then a smile, and the house is cleaner for knowing.

choices.text: Defend the register

effects.log: You defend it. The descendant goes away cold, and the gossip, which was right, goes on being right in the corners.

events.text: A grandchild of {b3_peer} has been found to have no talent whatever for the house arts, which is a minor tragedy and a major comedy. The child is cheerful, kind, cannot swing a sword, cannot hold a brush, cannot find the kitchen. The child is, nevertheless, the best-loved person in the house.

choices.text: Make the child the house host

effects.log: The child becomes the house host, greeting every guest with a kind, bewildered welcome. The visitors say it is the warmest house they know.

choices.text: Send the child for training in a gentler art

effects.log: The child is sent away to learn gardening, and comes back very good. The house has never looked so well.

events.text: A rumour goes round that {b3_clan} has hidden a treasure, left by the founder, somewhere in the walls. Treasure-hunters have appeared, politely, with maps. {b3_peer} has been seen tapping at the plaster. {b3_elder} says the only treasure in the walls is damp.

choices.text: Tell everyone it is damp, and mean it

effects.log: You tell everyone it is damp. Some are disappointed, and some, charmed by the candour, stay on as friends.

choices.text: Let the hunt run; it is amusing

effects.log: You let it run. Nothing is found but a very old child's toy and two coins, and the house puts them in the Cloud Tablet hall with a small label.

events.text: The head of a neighbouring house has fallen out with its own blood, and appears at your gate in the rain, asking for shelter, with a cloak and a trunk. The neighbour's blood send messages demanding the return. Everything about the matter is awkward, and a little, to the house's secret shame, thrilling.

choices.text: Give them shelter, and ask nothing

effects.log: You give shelter and ask nothing. The neighbour stays a season, mends with their blood by letter, and goes home, and your house is thereafter forgiven anything.

choices.text: Send word to their blood and let them settle it

effects.log: You send word. The blood arrives, and the argument is conducted in your parlour with extraordinary politeness and some broken crockery.

events.text: A foundling is left in the cloud court of {b3_clan} at dawn, wrapped in a good cloth with no crest on it. {b3_elder} says every house has one, and the ones who get kept are the ones who are noticed. {b3_peer} says the child is a spy in swaddling. The child, awake, regards you with great calm.

choices.text: Keep the child in the house, as one of its own

effects.log: The child is given a bed in the nursery and a name from the register of the blessed, and {b3_elder} sings badly in the corridor at night.

choices.text: Place the child with a good family nearby

effects.log: The child goes to a good family a short walk from the gate, and you watch from the wall for years.

events.text: The foundling of {b3_clan} has grown into a quick, careful young one with a gift for sums and for listening at doors. {b3_peer} has started treating the young one as an equal, which is the worst possible sign. Others of the blood resent it. The young one asks to sit at the table on feast days.

choices.text: Give them a seat, low on the bench

effects.log: The seat is low, and the young one is grateful beyond words. The blood mutter, and the matter is settled by the first feast, at which the young one pours the wine well.

choices.text: Say that the table is for the blood

effects.log: You say it kindly. The young one nods, never asks again, and is quieter, and keeps the books of the house with silent perfection.

events.text: The foundling of {b3_clan}, grown, has come to the study with a question: whose child were they? It is known, as it happens, to {b3_elder}, who has said nothing for thirty years, and who now stands at the door with a face like a closed book. A great house, it seems, once lost a child.

choices.text: Tell the truth, and let the young one go to their blood

effects.log: You tell the truth. The young one goes to the great house for a year and comes home to {b3_clan} by choice, with a gift and a promise, to the enormous relief of {b3_elder}.

choices.text: Tell the truth, and ask the young one to stay

effects.log: You ask the young one to stay, and the young one does, and the house is the stronger for a loyalty that was given and not owed.

choices.text: Keep it from them, as the old one wished

effects.log: You keep it. The young one never knows, and lives out a good life in the house, and {b3_elder} dies easy.

events.text: {b3_peer} stands up in the Cloud Tablet hall, in front of all the blood, and says in a trembling voice that the jade seal was never yours to keep. It is a speech clearly meant for a long time. {b3_elder} bows an old head. Half the room looks at the floor. The other half looks at you.

choices.text: Answer in the open, on the record

effects.log: You answer in the open, point by point. It is a long afternoon. {b3_peer} sits down red and unbowed, an opponent now by name.

choices.text: Embrace {b3_peer} and offer a seat on the council

effects.log: You cross the hall and embrace {b3_peer}, which no one expected, and offer a seat. {b3_peer} accepts, stiffly, and is a better ally than they were a foe.

events.text: {b3_peer} has gone from the house in the night with a dozen of the younger blood and a cart of the good bedding. A note says only that there is a house for those who were never asked. It is a very small, very sharp note. {b3_elder} says the dozen include some of the best the house has.

choices.text: Let them go, and wish them well in writing

effects.log: You write a warm, brief letter and send a fund of travelling money. The dozen are astonished. In a decade, some return.

choices.text: Send {b3_elder} after them with an offer

effects.log: {b3_elder} follows, and finds them in an inn by the river. Seven return; five go on, and do well, and keep a grudge.

events.text: A letter comes from {b3_peer}, now at the head of a house of dissidents, proposing that the two houses be joined, with {b3_peer} the equal of you, or else met in a trial before the neighbouring houses. It is flattering, and a threat, and in the same fine handwriting you remember from a childhood of arguments.

choices.text: Accept the union

effects.log: You accept. It is a long, difficult marriage of houses, and the old grievances are the first thing to be put on the table and the last to be settled. By the end the house is double its size.

choices.text: Accept the trial, and win it on the facts

effects.log: You accept the trial. The neighbouring houses hear both and find for yours, courteously. {b3_peer} bows, withdraws, and sends, a decade later, a wedding gift.

choices.text: Decline both, and return the old note, framed

effects.log: You decline both, and return the note in a frame. {b3_peer} takes it, and the silence that follows is not unfriendly.

events.text: A neighbouring house asks {b3_clan} for a loan against its orchard, as its roof is falling in. The house is proud, and has named the sum quietly, with a hand that shakes. It is an old house, and old houses have long memories for how they were treated when poor.

choices.text: Lend it freely, and ask for nothing in return

effects.log: You lend it freely. The neighbour weeps in the study, in the old way, with dignity, and the roof is mended in the spring.

choices.text: Lend it against the orchard, in writing

effects.log: You lend it against the orchard, with a fair term. It is a business, and the neighbour is relieved by its coolness.

events.text: The neighbour house, a few years on, has failed to make its payment, and its steward comes to your gate with the look of someone who has rehearsed in the mirror. The house has had a bad harvest, and a worse head. Their steward offers the orchard outright.

choices.text: Forgive the debt and take no orchard

effects.log: You forgive the debt. The steward kneels, and the neighbour house gives you, in years to come, a loyalty that cannot be bought.

choices.text: Take the orchard, and let them stay as tenants

effects.log: You take the orchard and let them stay, at a low rent. It is lawful and quiet, and the old house hates you in a courteous, patient way.

events.text: It is a hard year, and {b3_clan} has gone short. A train of loaded carts arrives from the neighbouring house with no note beyond a single line: the debt is remembered. They have come, unasked, with grain. The steward will not meet your eye, from sheer pride.

choices.text: Receive the grain with open thanks

effects.log: You receive it with open thanks. The neighbouring house is flushed with pleasure, and the two houses are, from that day, a single family in all but name.

choices.text: Receive it, and send a gift of the same weight in spring

effects.log: You send the same weight in spring. It is your way of saying that you do not take charity, and it is understood, and honoured.

events.text: At {b3_house} they ask your name, then your teacher's name, then the name of your teacher's teacher, and write all three down, in a hand that is pleasant and unhurried. It is how they decide where to seat you. The steward waits, pen lifted, with the look of someone who has seen a great many third answers.

choices.text: Give all three names, truthfully

effects.log: You give them all. The pen stops at the third, and the steward, for the first time, looks up.

choices.text: Say your own name is the only one that matters

effects.log: The steward writes it down, very slowly, and you are shown to the side bench by a person who is never seen again.

events.text: You are given tea in {b3_house}, in a cup with a hairline crack. It is either an oversight or a test, and nobody is going to say which. The household is watching, from windows, with the polite stillness of those who risk nothing aloud. The tea is very good.

choices.text: Drink it without remark

effects.log: You drink it to the last leaf, and set the cup down on the crack's own side. A maid, somewhere, lets out a breath.

choices.text: Remark gently on the crack

effects.log: You remark on it. The household is a moment silent, and then someone laughs, and it is not clear whether it was the right answer.

choices.text: Ask for a different cup

effects.log: You ask for another cup. It is brought at once, with a face of stone, and you are not asked back soon.

events.text: The young heir of {b3_house} meets you in the cloud court, and has been told to be civil, and manages it for the length of one sentence. The sentence is about how few outsiders get as far as this courtyard. The heir has a very good coat and has never been wrong aloud.

choices.text: Congratulate the heir on the coat

effects.log: You compliment the coat with total sincerity. The heir blinks, softens, and tells you where it was made, and the rest of the visit is easier.

choices.text: Out-talk the heir on the question of outsiders

ok.log: You answer so lightly and so well that the heir is left laughing in the middle of the courtyard, and a dozen servants pretend not to see.

fail.log: You answer too sharply. The heir goes quiet and white, and the house will remember a guest who was clever at it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and look at the garden

effects.log: You look at the garden. It is a good garden. The heir cannot decide whether this is an insult, and tells no one.

events.text: A very old aunt of {b3_house} is carried into the room, looks at you for a long while, and announces to the company that you have the nose of a person she once knew, in a different century, and did not like. The company holds still. The aunt is, by all accounts, rarely wrong.

choices.text: Say you hope to improve on the original

effects.log: The aunt barks a laugh, and the company breaks into relieved, nervous mirth. She asks you to sit beside her.

choices.text: Ask who she means

effects.log: She tells you at length, and the story is very bad, and you listen, and are thanked for it by all the house, later, in small ways.

choices.text: Bow, and say it was not you

effects.log: You say, with great courtesy, that it was not you. The aunt says nothing at all, and the company goes back to its tea.

events.text: You are shown the portraits of the heads of {b3_house}, one after another, down a long gallery, and each has the same chin. The steward speaks of them as if they were in the next room. At the end hangs a frame, empty. "Reserved," says the steward, with a very small smile.

choices.text: Ask whom it is reserved for

effects.log: The steward says only that the house is patient. You are not sure whether that was a joke, or a warning, or an invitation.

choices.text: Admire the chin, sincerely

effects.log: You admire the chin. The steward says it is considered the house's chief accomplishment, and the gallery warms by several degrees.

choices.text: Say the empty frame is the best one

effects.log: The steward does not smile, but a younger servant, behind, chokes. You are watched until you leave.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} will see you, but not yet, and not in the hall. You are shown to a bench in a passage where servants pass with trays. It is an hour before anyone speaks, and then only to ask whether you would like water. It is a very long hour, and very deliberate.

choices.text: Wait it out with a quiet face

effects.log: You wait it out. When the head at last appears they say, without preamble, that most guests leave by the second hour.

choices.text: Rise and walk out at the half-hour

effects.log: You walk out. A servant runs after you with a flustered apology, and a message that the head is now free, and you do not go back that day.

events.text: At supper in {b3_house}, you are placed one seat below where the guest of rank would sit, and one above where a petitioner would. It is a seat with no name, invented for you, and every person at the table knows its exact meaning. The soup is excellent.

choices.text: Take the seat and eat well

effects.log: You take the seat and eat well. The table watches you eat, and at the second course a cousin begins, cautiously, to talk to you.

choices.text: Ask, mildly, where the guest of rank sits

effects.log: You ask. It is a perfectly polite question, and it is as if you had dropped a plate. The seat is changed, and so is the house's opinion.

events.text: A tournament of manners is held in {b3_house} on the day you call, though it is not called that. Guests bow, are bowed to, pour, are poured for, and each small gesture is scored by an old woman in the corner with a fan. Your turn comes. The fan stops moving.

choices.text: Play it with grace

ok.log: You play every gesture a hair's breadth early and a hair's breadth modest. The fan, to general amazement, folds, and the old woman nods once.

fail.log: You mis-pour, by a thumb, and the entire room sees it. The fan resumes, and it is a long, kind, merciless evening.

choices.text: Decline to be scored, with a smile

effects.log: You say you are not here to be scored. A murmur, and the old woman's fan makes a gesture you cannot read. You are not asked again.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} has a custom: every visitor must name one thing in the house that is better than where they come from. It is a custom meant to flatter, and also to catch liars. You have been in the house for twenty minutes, and the whole family is waiting.

choices.text: Name the garden, and mean it

effects.log: You name the garden and describe three plants in it. A gardener, behind a hedge, is overheard saying, "At last."

choices.text: Name the kitchen, with detail

effects.log: You name the kitchen, and the smell of the third bread. The whole family eats earlier than usual.

choices.text: Say the house is exactly as good as anywhere

effects.log: You say so, with honest intent. It is the most insulting thing anyone has said under that roof in forty years, and also, a little, admired.

events.text: You are asked at {b3_house}, over a very long meal, to settle a quarrel between two cousins, neither of whom will say what it is about. The house has been waiting some time for an outsider with no side. Both cousins look at you with great hope and some contempt.

choices.text: Hear them separately, and say what you think

effects.log: You hear them separately. They have quarrelled over a borrowed horse, a lost letter and a slight, in that order. You say what you think, and they are both furious, and fair.

choices.text: Decline; it is a house matter

effects.log: You decline, with courtesy. The cousins are left with each other, and the house with an outsider who did not overreach.

choices.text: Tell them to settle it with a game

effects.log: You tell them to settle it with a game of stones. The house is shocked, and then not, and then the game is long, and the horse is returned.

events.text: A young person of {b3_house} slips out from behind a pillar and asks if you are the one who is not afraid of the old ones. The young one has clearly been told you were. It is flattering and a little frightening, for the child's eyes are very serious and the house is full of ears.

choices.text: Say you are afraid, a little, of everyone

effects.log: The child is enchanted by this. It becomes, by dinner, a house story, told with exaggeration, and it helps you.

choices.text: Say yes, with a grin

effects.log: The child grins back, and runs off, and the old ones, hearing, are less amused than the child.

events.text: There is a path through the grounds of {b3_house} that guests may not walk, though no sign says so. You are shown the other, longer path, by a servant who says nothing about it. At the turning you can see the forbidden one, and a figure sitting on a bench at its end, unmoving.

choices.text: Keep to the long path, and look away

effects.log: You keep to the long path. The figure on the bench, as you turn, lifts a hand, once, very slowly. You do not ask.

choices.text: Step onto the forbidden path, a few paces

effects.log: You step onto it. A servant arrives from nowhere with a very calm face. You are told it is only a path, and it is the longest walk of your life.

events.text: The women of {b3_house} gather in the garden room, every afternoon, and an invitation there is a kind of promotion. You have not got one. The steward mentions this, as a weather fact. Beyond the screen, a laugh; a good, round one. You have also heard it said that the house is run from this room.

choices.text: Send flowers, without a card

effects.log: You send flowers, without a card. The next day a note comes back with a single word, and it is the right one, and you are invited.

choices.text: Wait to be asked

effects.log: You wait. You are not asked, that year. The house notes you did not push, and the not-asking is quietly revised.

events.text: You have been told by three different people, at {b3_house}, that the founder was a great man, and by none of them what he did. A fourth, a very old gardener, tells you the founder was a very bad-tempered man who liked beans. You like the gardener at once.

choices.text: Sit with the gardener, and talk beans

effects.log: You sit with the gardener all afternoon. It turns out the house's true history is in beans, and the gardener gives you a packet of seed. It is a prized thing.

choices.text: Say nothing; the gardener is unauthorised

effects.log: You say nothing. The gardener nods, as if expecting it, and goes back to work, and the house never knows.

events.text: A brother and sister of {b3_house} finish each other's sentences, which is unsettling in company, and spend dinner explaining the family to you in alternating phrases. They are clever, and bored, and clearly fond of you. They have a plan for you, and they have not decided what it is.

choices.text: Ask them what the plan is

effects.log: They look at each other with alarm and delight. The plan, it emerges, is to marry you off to a cousin, and they have a list. You decline with gratitude.

choices.text: Let them go on; it is entertaining

effects.log: You let them go on, and by the end you know every secret of the house, and they know you did not use any.

events.text: You are taken at {b3_house} to the library, and shown the shelves of the house's own writings, which fill three walls. The librarian, who has read every one, takes a book down and holds it out as one hands over an infant. "It is very bad," the librarian says, quietly, "but it is ours."

choices.text: Read the first pages, and say what is good in it

effects.log: You find a good page and say so. The librarian's eyes fill. It is, you suspect, the first time in years anyone has read it, and word of it spreads.

choices.text: Ask for a different book

effects.log: The librarian gives you a different one, graciously, and says nothing of the first.

events.text: The steward of {b3_house} shows you the crest of the house, and the crest of each of the eight branches, and the story of every crest, in sequence, and the cadet crests, and the lapsed. By the thirty-first, you are quite certain you are being tested for patience. The steward knows it too.

choices.text: Listen through to the last crest

effects.log: You listen through. The steward, at the end, is very nearly moved, and offers you the one crest not shown to guests, a plain unpainted board.

choices.text: Ask for the shortest version of the family

effects.log: You ask for the short version. The steward gives it, in one sentence, with admirable economy, and it is perfectly true.

events.text: A cousin of {b3_house}, resentful of the house, takes you aside and says that everyone here is a hypocrite, and wants to tell you who. It is a wonderful afternoon. You are told a good many things, some of them true, and all of them very bad for the house if repeated.

choices.text: Hear it, and repeat nothing

effects.log: You hear it, and repeat nothing. The cousin, a week later, sends you a small gift and a letter that is far too frank, and it is a kind of trust.

choices.text: Hear it, and carry some of it back as a warning

effects.log: You carry some of it back, tactfully. The house is grateful and sharp-eyed, and the cousin is hurt.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} receives you standing, which is an honour, and does not offer a seat, which is a different one. For a long minute the two of you are in the same room, looking at the same wall. Then the head says that an honest guest is a rare ornament, and asks what you want.

choices.text: Say you want nothing the house cannot spare

effects.log: The head half-smiles. It is a good answer, and expensive, and the head will be wondering about the price for the rest of the year.

choices.text: Say you want a seat

effects.log: A seat is brought. It is a very good seat, and the head sits on a lesser one, and you are not sure who has won.

choices.text: Say you came to see the garden

effects.log: The head is silent, then amused, and sends for a gardener, and an hour of the day is yours in the garden.

events.text: A visiting scholar of {b3_house}, in the middle of a lecture, stops mid-sentence and says that you, specifically, are an insult to the study of the founders. It is a fine, ringing insult. It is a thing the house does to guests, to see how they take it. The room is very quiet.

choices.text: Ask the scholar to explain how

effects.log: You ask. The scholar, taken aback, explains, at length, and is wrong in two places, and you correct them gently. A small, startled applause breaks out at the back.

choices.text: Laugh, and say you hope to be a bigger one

effects.log: You laugh, and say so. The room laughs with relief, and the scholar, grudgingly, bows.

choices.text: Stand and leave in silence

effects.log: You leave in silence, and the house is ashamed for an afternoon, and also cold to you for a decade.

events.text: In {b3_house}, you are asked to bring a gift, and then told it is not necessary, and then asked why you have not. It is a house where each of these is perfectly consistent. You have, as it happens, brought a small present, of no great price, and the household has seen you carrying it.

choices.text: Offer it plainly

effects.log: You offer it plainly. It is a small thing, a plain object, and the house treats it with great gravity, and keeps it where visitors can see it.

choices.text: Keep it, and give it to a servant instead

effects.log: You give it to a kitchen servant. The head hears of it before supper and says nothing, in a way that is not quite displeasure.

events.text: The doorkeeper of {b3_house} makes you wait by a stone lion, and tells you that the lion is a better judge of character than the house. The lion has a worn paw where people have patted it for luck. The doorkeeper has been at the gate for decades and has opinions on everyone.

choices.text: Pat the lion's paw

effects.log: You pat the paw. The doorkeeper looks, grudgingly, almost pleased, and lets you in by the near door.

choices.text: Ask the doorkeeper what he thinks of the house

effects.log: You ask. The doorkeeper tells you in four dry sentences, and one is a secret, and you are admitted by the side door with something like friendship.

events.text: You find, at {b3_house}, that a seat has been kept for you at a table where no one is sitting. An uneasy servant explains that this is where guests of no clear standing are placed, so that the house can decide at leisure. Across the room, the head of the house is watching you, and has stopped chewing.

choices.text: Sit in it, and be unremarkable

effects.log: You sit, eat modestly, speak little. By the sweet course a few have drifted over, and the head has quite lost interest, which is the best thing.

choices.text: Cross the room and sit by the head

effects.log: You cross the room and sit by the head, uninvited. It is either audacity or ignorance, and the house is for a time unsure which, and so are you.

events.text: The musicians of {b3_house} are said to be the best on the isle. A visitor is asked, by custom, to sing. You have never sung in public. A very small servant is handing round a tray of cups to the audience, and a very grand one has found you the best chair for the purpose.

choices.text: Sing, badly and with conviction

ok.log: You sing a country song with entirely too much conviction and no grace, and the house, by the second verse, has joined in. It is the happiest evening of the year.

fail.log: You forget the second verse, and sing the first again, louder. The silence is complete. Later someone says it was brave.

choices.text: Ask to hear the house sing instead

effects.log: You ask the house to sing, and they do, and are ravishing, and you have been a good guest.

events.text: A great-uncle of {b3_house} has noticed that you are well-spoken, and has decided that you must hear every opinion he has ever held, in order. It is a captive audience of one. The family watches from doors with a sympathy that stops very precisely at the doorframe.

choices.text: Listen, and ask a good question each hour

effects.log: You listen, and ask a question each hour. By dusk he is calling you his friend, and the family can hardly believe it, and are quietly grateful.

choices.text: Excuse yourself at the second hour

effects.log: You excuse yourself gently. He is wounded for a day and delighted again by morning, and the house is neutral.

events.text: You are late to {b3_house}: a road, a lamed beast, an apology you have been rehearsing since dawn. The house has dined. They set a place anyway, for a meal already cold, with the stiff courtesy of people who consider lateness a character fault. A child watches you eat, solemnly.

choices.text: Apologise fully, and eat the cold food gladly

effects.log: You apologise, and eat. The head, from the end of the table, says they have been late themselves, once, to a worse place, and the cold is forgotten.

choices.text: Apologise briefly, and ask about the family

effects.log: You apologise briefly, and ask about the family. It is deft, and the child, watching, takes your side.

events.text: A very fine duel of calligraphy is proposed, and refused, and proposed again, as a courtesy, in {b3_house}. It is not a contest of strength. It is a contest of ink, with a famed old brush as prize. You are not asked to take part. You are asked only to judge, which is much worse.

choices.text: Judge it fairly, and say why

effects.log: You judge it fairly, and give three reasons. The loser thanks you, and the winner is curt, and the house trusts you the more.

choices.text: Declare it a draw, with a compliment to both

effects.log: You declare a draw. It is accepted with perfect politeness and a certain feeling that you were afraid.

events.text: The kitchen of {b3_house} sends out a dish you have never seen, and the household falls silent to see what you do. It is the house's old test of a guest: the dish is, by tradition, very bitter. The cook is standing at the door with a cloth in her hands, shaking slightly.

choices.text: Eat it all, and ask for the name of the herb

effects.log: You eat it all, and it is dreadful, and you ask for the herb. The cook weeps, and the household cheers, and it is, quietly, the best thing you will do there.

choices.text: Eat a little, and say it is a taste to learn

effects.log: You eat a little, and say it is a taste to learn. The cook is amused, and the house is evenly divided.

events.text: You are shown the bedchamber prepared for you in {b3_house}. It has a view, a very good bed, and, you realise, a window that looks directly across the cloud court into the study of the head. Nothing is said. There is, by the bed, a small bell. The steward bows.

choices.text: Close the shutters, courteously

effects.log: You close the shutters, and the steward is, by the evening, much more at ease. The head is unoffended, even a little relieved.

choices.text: Leave the shutters open, and sleep soundly

effects.log: You leave them open, and sleep. In the morning the head, at breakfast, says the light was on late in the study, and so was yours, and we are alike.

events.text: It is the anniversary of a death in {b3_house}, and you have called on the worst day. The whole house is in white, and moves about like water. No one tells you to leave. No one tells you to stay. A small boy brings you a cup of something warm and sits down next to you without a word.

choices.text: Stay, and sit the vigil with them

effects.log: You stay through the night. The family says nothing of it, then or ever, and a year later you receive a single white flower from the head.

choices.text: Withdraw quietly, and send a note

effects.log: You withdraw quietly, and send a note. It is correct, and received, and not remembered.

events.text: At {b3_house} you are twice mistaken for someone else, once as a tutor and once as a creditor. Both are met with unnerving politeness. The third time, a very old man looks at you hard and says that the face is right but the manners are wrong, and you are, he is sure, a spy.

choices.text: Say that you are exactly that, and a poor one

effects.log: You say you are a poor one. The old man roars with laughter and tells the whole house, and it works wonders.

choices.text: Insist you are a plain guest

effects.log: You insist. The old man nods wisely, as if that is what a spy would say, and you are watched with respect.

events.text: A rival of {b3_house}, also a guest, has been seated beside you. They are courteous, brilliant, and a clear spy, and you can see them thinking the same of you. The whole supper is a long slow dance of the unsaid. By the sweet course, the head of the house is very amused.

choices.text: Share a small, true thing with the rival

effects.log: You share a small true thing. The rival is nonplussed, shares one back, and for the rest of the night you are collaborators in the enjoyment of the head.

choices.text: Let the rival do all the talking

effects.log: You let them talk. By midnight they have told you a great deal and you have told them nothing, and the head notes it.

events.text: Every wall in {b3_house} has a hole in it somewhere, from some ancient quarrel, and each has been plastered over in a slightly different colour. The tour is a history of tempers. The steward is almost fond of them. At the last wall, a very small, very new crack, and the steward stops.

choices.text: Ask about the new crack

effects.log: The steward tells you, low: the head, last month, in a rage, over a letter. It is a confidence, given freely, and you are trusted.

choices.text: Pretend not to see it

effects.log: You pretend not to see. The steward breathes out, and you are, for the rest of the tour, a model guest.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} keeps, in its hall, a bell that rings by itself whenever someone with a hidden grievance enters. It has not rung for a hundred years. As you cross the threshold, a servant, by the door, closes both eyes tightly, and the bell is silent. There is a very long pause.

choices.text: Say you are glad it is silent

effects.log: You say you are glad. The servant opens his eyes, and a whole household, behind the doors, breathes out, and you do not mention the bell again.

choices.text: Ask what the bell is for

effects.log: You ask. The tale is long and half-true and delightful, and the steward is, at the end, quite pleased with you.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} asks, at your leave-taking, what you thought of the house. It is the question the whole visit has been building to. It is an examination, you realise, and the answer is being awaited by the steward, the aunt, the cook, the child and several unseen listeners.

choices.text: Say it is a house that remembers well

effects.log: The head nods slowly. That is the highest praise the house recognises, and the steward, behind you, relaxes.

choices.text: Say it is a house that forgets nothing, and forgives little

effects.log: The head is silent, and then says that is the truest thing a guest has said in years. It is not clear whether you are forgiven for it.

choices.text: Say you found it a little cold

effects.log: You say so. The head accepts it gravely, and in the morning a fire has been lit in your room, and the house has a new regard for you.

events.text: You have called on {b3_house} too often, or so it seems from the steward's tone. "A frequent guest," the steward says, "is either a friend or a project." It is said lightly, and without malice, and the steward is waiting for you to choose which.

choices.text: Say friend, and mean it

effects.log: You say friend. The steward considers, writes something in a small book, and the house, for a time, does you small kindnesses.

choices.text: Say project, with a smile

effects.log: You say project, and the steward laughs aloud, and says the house is rather one itself, and a bargain is understood.

events.text: A servant of {b3_house} takes you aside in a back passage and says quietly that if you are here to ask for anything, the day to ask is not today. It is unsolicited, kind, and probably dangerous for the servant. The head, they say, is in a mood, and the reason is a piece of news you have not heard.

choices.text: Thank the servant, and defer your request

effects.log: You defer. The servant is quietly proud, the head is grateful for your tact when the matter surfaces, and a tiny alliance is made below stairs.

choices.text: Ask what the news is

effects.log: The servant tells you, in a few words. It is bad, and it is a house secret, and you carry it with great care.

events.text: The grand stair of {b3_house} has ninety steps, and you are required to climb them alone, because guests are. Halfway up you realise the steps are slightly uneven, a deliberate design: to make each climber arrive winded, humble, and slightly late. At the top, the head waits and does not look winded.

choices.text: Take the stair at a calm pace

ok.log: You climb it steadily, and arrive composed. The head glances at your breathing, and almost nods.

fail.log: You arrive winded, and the head waits, perfectly composed, as the whole house watches from the windows.

choices.text: Stop and rest on the fortieth step

effects.log: You rest on the fortieth step. Someone, somewhere, says that is the first time a guest has done that, and it is spoken of kindly.

events.text: {b3_house} takes gifts seriously. Yours, a modest one, has been put on a stand in the entrance, and a small card written beside it, by the steward, in the finest hand. The card says what you intended. It says it much better than you did.

choices.text: Ask the steward to write the card for your next gift too

effects.log: The steward is, you can see, enormously pleased. The two of you are, from that moment, a small conspiracy.

choices.text: Say the card is better than the gift

effects.log: The steward goes pink. It is true, and said gracefully, and the whole house hears of it.

events.text: You are made to wait at {b3_house} among the other petitioners in a long hall, and it is instructive. There is a woman with a child, an old man with a roll of paper, and a young lawyer in a coat too good for his purse. Each tells you a different version of the house, and each is partly true.

choices.text: Share your tea with the old man and the child

effects.log: You share your tea. The head, passing through, sees you with the child on your knee, and later the steward says the head has noted it.

choices.text: Compare notes with the young lawyer
