effects.log: You compare notes with the lawyer, and learn the house's five weaknesses, and the lawyer is, after, a friend of yours for life.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} shows you the family tree, a monstrous thing, painted on a dozen scrolls. Your name is not on it. A branch has been left, you notice, quite deliberately blank. "In case," says the head, and rolls the scroll up, and says no more.

choices.text: Say nothing, and look at the head steadily

effects.log: You say nothing. The head looks away first, a thing no one in the house has seen, and the scroll is put back with unusual care.

choices.text: Ask what the blank branch is for

effects.log: The head says it is for whoever the house is wrong about. It is a good line, and it is meant, and you remember it for a very long time.

events.text: A memory of {b3_house} is brought out and set before you like a dish: a slight, a century or three ago, done by your teacher's teacher to the house's founder. The head tells it with perfect calm, and then asks how you propose to settle it. The whole room is waiting.

choices.text: Apologise, on behalf of a name that is not yours

effects.log: You apologise, gravely and without reserve. The head is startled, and then moved, and the apology is written into the house books and never revoked.

choices.text: Say the dead cannot be made to answer

effects.log: You say it, and it is true. The head says that is what everyone says, and it is a cold comfort, and the room is a little less friendly.

choices.text: Offer a gift of the teacher's own school in settlement

effects.log: You offer a scroll, a good one, from the old school. It is accepted with no thanks and a very long, careful look.

events.text: An unexpected storm keeps you a night in {b3_house}, and the whole house, grudgingly, is made kind. Blankets arrive. A hot bowl. A very old man, who turns out to be the head's father, sits up with you, and says nothing for three hours, and then tells you the one thing worth knowing about the house.

choices.text: Listen with all your attention

effects.log: You listen. It is a sentence only, about the founder's doubt, and you do not repeat it, and it is, in the morning, the reason the head greets you as a friend.

choices.text: Fall asleep, in the middle

effects.log: You fall asleep, ashamed. The old man covers you with the blanket, and says in the morning that he has never had a better listener.

events.text: Three servants at {b3_house} each, separately, ask you to carry a letter out of the house, and each begs you not to tell the others. It is a very busy house, in its secret life. The letters are small, in several hands, and the three servants, you suspect, are working for three different people.

choices.text: Carry none, and say why to each

effects.log: You carry none, and say why. The three servants are, to the last, ashamed and relieved, and the house is quietly better run.

choices.text: Carry all three, and read nothing

effects.log: You carry them all and read nothing. You are, for a while, in a very curious position in the houses of the district.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} proposes, as a gesture of courtesy, a game of long chess with you: one move a day, for a year, played by courier. It is an honour, and a trap, and a serious commitment. Both are standing at the board, waiting.

choices.text: Accept, and play it with all your care

effects.log: You accept, and play the year. At the end it is a draw, and the head sends you the board, which is a thing of great beauty, and a note of two words.

choices.text: Accept, and play it for fun

effects.log: You play for fun. The head is, at first, offended, then charmed, and the game, with its mistakes, is one of the great correspondences of the age.

choices.text: Decline with all courtesy

effects.log: You decline, and the head says only, "Of course," and you have the sense of a door closing gently.

events.text: You are made known, at {b3_house}, to a gaggle of young people who treat you with the particular ease of those who have never had to earn anything. They ask you a great many questions, some insolent, one or two intelligent. One asks, frankly, what it is like to have to try.

choices.text: Answer honestly, with a good story

effects.log: You answer honestly, with the story of a long failure. They are silent, and then, to your surprise, serious, and one or two of them, years later, find you.

choices.text: Turn the question back on them

effects.log: You ask what it is like not to. It is a difficult moment, and a revealing one, and the youngest laughs.

events.text: You spend a year in the service of {b3_house}, and the first season is all errands. You carry letters, and learn who may be sent a letter and who may not. By autumn you could draw the house's quarrels on a map, and the steward, who has not smiled in your presence, asks whether you can keep a secret.

choices.text: Say you can, and keep one

effects.log: You keep it, a small one, about a debt. In a year it is confirmed, and the steward's regard is a quiet, solid thing.

choices.text: Say it depends on the secret

effects.log: The steward considers this, and says it is the right answer, and gives you the bigger errands and none of the secrets.

events.text: In the service of {b3_house}, you are sent to hold a tenant's lease to the letter, against a poor family. It is within the house's right. It is also a grief. The steward says the head will be glad of it, and in a tone that suggests the head may not be told.

choices.text: Hold the lease, kindly, and add a grace term

effects.log: You hold it and add a grace term of your own. The steward says nothing, and the family stays, and your account is a little overdrawn.

choices.text: Hold the lease to the letter

effects.log: You hold it to the letter. The family goes, and the house is richer, and you are spoken of as reliable, and do not feel well.

choices.text: Quietly tell the head the facts

effects.log: You tell the head. The head frowns, and cancels the lease, and gives you a long, odd look that is not quite approval.

events.text: A year in {b3_house} teaches you its hierarchy of silences. There is the silence of the head, and of the steward, and of the aunts, and each says something different. You are learning to read them as one reads weather. By winter, the silence of the cook is the one that matters most.

choices.text: Befriend the cook

effects.log: You befriend the cook, with small, practical favours. By spring the house's news reaches you before it reaches the steward.

choices.text: Keep to your own duties, and listen

effects.log: You keep to your duties and listen. You come out of the year knowing everything and with no obligations at all, and with a few cold looks.

events.text: The Cloud Tablet hall of {b3_house} is to be repaired, and you are placed in charge of the work, because the house will not spend its own people on it. It is a thankless post. The workmen quarrel. The beams are rotten. The steward visits every day, silently, and writes in a small book.

choices.text: Do it properly, and slowly

effects.log: You do it properly, and slowly. It is finished late and perfect, and the steward, to your amazement, says it is the first repair he has not had to see done twice.

choices.text: Do it fast, and cheaply

effects.log: You do it fast and cheap. It stands, and the steward says nothing, and it is repaired again in ten years, by someone else.

events.text: You serve in {b3_house} as a tutor of the young for a year. They are spoiled, quick, and unkind to each other in the way of the well-fed. One, the quietest, is being bullied by the rest, and does nothing about it. The house considers this a good way to learn.

choices.text: Intervene, quietly, and teach the quiet one a defence

effects.log: You teach the quiet one a defence. By spring the bullies have found another game, and the quiet one is your devoted friend for life.

choices.text: Let the house's custom run

effects.log: You let it run. The quiet one learns, in the end, what the house meant them to, and is not grateful, and is formidable.

events.text: It is a year of bad harvests, and {b3_house} asks you to oversee the stores. There is not enough, and every branch of the house claims priority. They come to you in turn: the aunts, the cousins, the cadets. It is the sort of work that makes enemies in the shape of friends.

choices.text: Divide the stores by need, and publish the division

effects.log: You divide by need and publish it, in the hall. It is accepted, grudgingly, and the house survives the winter with fewer quarrels than any in memory.

choices.text: Favour the main branch, as custom wants

effects.log: You favour the main branch. The house survives, and the cadets remember, and you do not sleep well.

events.text: You hold the door of {b3_house} through a siege of petty insults: a rival house's servants, every night, hurl a rotten pear, a rude song, a bad drawing. It is not a real siege. It is a game of endurance. The head says, politely, that the house expects its door-holder to win.

choices.text: Answer the rudeness with courtesy each night

effects.log: You answer with courtesy each night, and bring out a pot of tea. By the fortieth night the rival servants are drinking it, and the siege ends in a friendship.

choices.text: Answer in kind, with better songs

effects.log: You answer in kind, with better songs. The house is delighted, and the district enchanted, and the head quietly wounded.

events.text: Serving {b3_house}, you are sent as an envoy to a house the head despises, with a message the head does not mean. Both of you know the message is false. The other house's steward receives it with a grave bow, as if it were a gift, and says that the head is a great man and has a beautiful hand.

choices.text: Deliver it exactly, and say nothing more

effects.log: You deliver it exactly. The other steward gives you a look of perfect sympathy, and the correspondence continues, and you are valued for discretion.

choices.text: Add a quiet, true word of your own

effects.log: You add a true word. The other steward is moved, and the quarrel eases, and the head, angry at first, is eventually relieved.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} requires, for the year, that its servers eat in silence at a long table. You have never known such a quiet. After a month you can tell, by the sound of a spoon, who has had bad news. After two, you are the only one the others talk to, after supper, in the kitchen, in whispers.

choices.text: Keep what you are told

effects.log: You keep what you are told. It is a large, warm, heavy thing to hold, and by the end of the year the house cannot imagine a table without you.

choices.text: Use some of it, gently, to help

effects.log: You use some of it, gently. A debt is cleared, a rift mended, and no one knows the source, and it is a deep satisfaction.

events.text: A year in the service of {b3_house}, and the cousin who must be kept away from the wine has become, as these things go, your charge. You have learned the cousin's tricks: the borrowed cups, the friendly servants, the sudden headache. The cousin is funny, ruined, and quite aware of everything.

choices.text: Take the cousin on long walks, and out of the house

effects.log: You walk every evening. By spring the cousin is, by small steps, better, and writes you a note in a handwriting almost steady.

choices.text: Lock the cellar, and say nothing

effects.log: You lock the cellar. The cousin is furious for a season and silent for a year, and the house calls it a success, and it is not.

events.text: You serve {b3_house} for a year as its recorder, and in the third month find, in the archive, a letter that would ruin an entire branch. It is old, certainly true, and has been kept by a long line of recorders out of a sort of nervous piety. It is yours to keep or burn.

choices.text: Keep it, sealed, for the next recorder

effects.log: You seal it, and add a line of your own, and pass it on. It is the same fear, passed down, and you add your name to the line.

choices.text: Burn it, and say nothing

effects.log: You burn it. The branch is spared, and the line of recorders ends, and the archive, ever after, is ten degrees colder.

events.text: You serve at {b3_house}, and by midsummer it is clear the head is ill. Nobody says so. The steward moves lighter, the cook cooks gentler, the young speak low. You are asked, discreetly, to guard the head's door, and to turn away all visitors, including the heir.

choices.text: Guard the door, and turn them all away

effects.log: You guard it. It is a quiet, hard, honourable duty, and the head, at the end, thanks you in four words, and means each.

choices.text: Let the heir in, against orders

effects.log: You let the heir in. It is the right thing, and against orders, and the steward turns a blind eye, and it is not forgotten by anyone.

events.text: In the household of {b3_house} you teach swordplay to the cadets, and one of them, a fierce, unhappy child, wants only to be thrown out. The child provokes, insults, breaks. It is a plea, you realise, and a very old one. The steward says the house will do what you advise.

choices.text: Keep the child, and be patient

effects.log: You keep the child, patient as a wall. In two years the child is the house's best, and asks, without looking at you, if they may stay.

choices.text: Send the child away to another school

effects.log: You send the child away. It is done with care, and the child writes once a year, and always says thank you.

events.text: A year serving {b3_house} makes you the keeper of its calendar: births, funerals, feasts, the quiet date a branch once split. You find that two of the dates fall on the same day, and the house, by long custom, observes both with equal solemnity. You must choose.

choices.text: Hold both, one at dawn and one at dusk

effects.log: You hold both. The house is exhausted and moved, and the calendar is, ever after, kept this way.

choices.text: Move one by a day, quietly

effects.log: You move one by a day, quietly. No one notices for years, and then an old aunt does, and says nothing, and sends you a ribbon.

events.text: You spend a year at {b3_house} as the house's representative at a legal dispute with a neighbour over a stream. It is a thankless post; the case is old, the facts are thin, the other house's advocate is a master. Each night you rehearse. Each morning the steward looks at you with a stoic, kind fear.

choices.text: Argue it with all you have

ok.log: You argue it with all you have, and the neighbour's advocate, at the end, bows to you across the court. It is a draw, with honour, and the house is delighted.

fail.log: You argue it well, and lose, by a hair. The house is, to your surprise, kind, and the steward pats your arm.

choices.text: Propose a settlement at the first hearing

effects.log: You propose a settlement, and it is taken, quickly, to the relief of both. The house is not pleased, and not displeased.

events.text: You are made steward for a year of the house's great feast, and you learn that a feast is a war. The cooks, the musicians, the dancers, the table-setters, each have their own general. By the third week you are sleeping in a corridor. The head, passing, gives you a nod of ruthless sympathy.

choices.text: Run it like a campaign, with lists

effects.log: You run it with lists, and it goes off without a flaw, and the head says it was the best feast in a decade. You sleep for three days.

choices.text: Let each general run their own, and mediate

effects.log: You mediate. The feast is a glorious, noisy, uneven thing, and the guests love it, and the generals love you.

events.text: While you serve {b3_house}, a young person of the house falls in love with you, with the helpless clarity of the very young. It is touching and absurd. The house is aware of it, and the heir is aware of it, and the steward has moved your lodgings to the far wing, tactfully.

choices.text: Speak to the young one, kindly and plainly

effects.log: You speak plainly and kindly. The young one is crushed and then, within a season, almost grateful, and it is long remembered with gentleness.

choices.text: Avoid the matter, and hope

effects.log: You avoid it. It fades, awkwardly, over a year, and the house says nothing, and the young one avoids you forever.

events.text: You are put to guard the house treasury of {b3_house}, which is the storeroom of its pride: old gifts, old debts, a dozen things that cannot be sold and cannot be explained. On a quiet night a person you know, of the house, comes and asks, very politely, to borrow one thing.

choices.text: Refuse, and report it to the steward

effects.log: You refuse, and report. The person is dismissed from the treasury, and the house, privately, thinks you rigid, and deeply useful.

choices.text: Refuse, and say nothing to anyone

effects.log: You refuse, and say nothing. It is a very small mercy, and the person, ever after, is a quiet ally.

choices.text: Lend it, on the person's honour

effects.log: You lend it. It is returned in a week, and nothing happens, and the whole affair gives you a long, unlovely secret.

events.text: A year in {b3_house}, and the quarrel that frames the whole household, between two great-aunts, comes to a head over a recipe. You are, by accident, the only one who has eaten both versions. Each aunt wants your verdict. The kitchen is in suspense. The whole house is.

choices.text: Say they are both right, in different ways

effects.log: You say so, with specifics. Neither aunt is satisfied, and each is, secretly, flattered, and the kitchen produces both thereafter.

choices.text: Name one, honestly

effects.log: You name one, honestly. The other aunt will not speak to you for a year, and then sends you the recipe, with a note.

events.text: In the service of {b3_house} you are asked to escort a young one to a distant betrothal. It is a long, dull journey, with a reluctant bride-to-be who spends it asking about the world you know. By the last stage she asks whether she must go on. It is, in the house, not a question to be asked.

choices.text: Answer honestly: it is her choice, and what it would cost

effects.log: You answer honestly. She goes on, eyes open, and is a force in her new house, and writes to you every year.

choices.text: Say it is not for you to say, and deliver her

effects.log: You deliver her. It is correct, and the house is content, and you remember her face at the gate for a long time.

events.text: You serve {b3_house} for a year as its night watch, and the house at night is a different house. Doors open that never open by day. A very old man walks the corridor at three, talking to someone. A child sleeps in a chair. Nobody explains, and you learn not to ask.

choices.text: Walk with the old man a few nights

effects.log: You walk with him. He talks to his dead wife, and sometimes to you, and by spring you know the house's oldest secret, which is only that he was happy once.

choices.text: Keep to your round, and give them room

effects.log: You keep to your round, and the house is, in its odd way, grateful for the room you give.

events.text: You find that the bookkeeping of {b3_house} has been, for decades, kept in two hands, one for the true figures and one for the shown. It is an old, benign dishonesty, a gift to the creditors and a comfort to the pride. You are asked, by the steward, to take over the second hand.

choices.text: Take it, and keep the figures close to the truth

effects.log: You take it, and nudge the shown toward the true. The creditors are, eventually, impressed, and the steward breathes easier by the year.

choices.text: Refuse, and ask to keep only the true set

effects.log: You refuse. The steward bows, and the pride of the house is, from then on, a little poorer and a little cleaner.

events.text: A year serving {b3_house} teaches you that its peace depends entirely on a single plain woman, nobody important, who sits in the kitchen and listens to everyone. She is called Auntie and has no surname and no seat. When she falls ill the entire house is in a quiet panic. You are asked to find a remedy.

choices.text: Search out the best healer you can, at any cost

effects.log: You find a healer, a long way off, and bring her back. Auntie recovers, grumbling, and the house gives you a respect that costs it nothing and means a great deal.

choices.text: Sit with her yourself, through the nights

effects.log: You sit with her through the nights, and she tells you, in half-delirium, how the house is really governed. It is the best lesson of your life.

events.text: Serving {b3_house} as a courier you cross three isles of the old quarrel, carrying a very small, very sealed packet. At each crossing you are stopped, searched, bowed to, and sent on. At the last, a person in plain grey takes the packet, reads it, and weeps. You are never told why.

choices.text: Say nothing of it, ever

effects.log: You say nothing. The house knows, somehow, that you did not, and the head greets you thereafter like someone who has passed a test.

choices.text: Ask the head what was in it

effects.log: The head tells you, after a long pause. It is a fragment of a poem. You believe it matters, and the head believes you do.

events.text: In {b3_house}, you teach the young the rules of precedence, and find that the rules are inconsistent. Three of them cannot both be true. The young have noticed, and are delighted, and asking which to follow. The aunts, in the doorway, are very still.

choices.text: Say the rules are a poem, not a law

effects.log: You say it. The young laugh, the aunts do not, and you are invited to tea with the eldest the next day, and it is a very long tea.

choices.text: Tell the young to follow the oldest, always

effects.log: You say so. It is the safe answer, and the aunts nod, and the young, privately, think less of you.

events.text: You serve {b3_house} through the year of its great mourning, and learn that mourning is a craft: the white, the silence, the meals, the visits. You are given the visits. Each day, a different branch, a different grief. You carry the same cup, and the same few words, and it is, by the end, true.

choices.text: Say the words as if each time were the first

effects.log: You say them each time as new. The branches, in their grief, feel it, and you are loved by the house with a quiet, deep, unspoken thing.

choices.text: Vary the words, and offer an honest memory each time

effects.log: You offer a memory, each time, a small true one. The house is the more comforted, and you are tired in a way sleep does not cure.

events.text: You serve {b3_house} for a year as a go-between with its estranged sister-house. The two have not met in sixty years. You carry messages in both directions that are each, politely, an insult, and you learn to convert them in transit. By autumn they are, with your help, almost civil.

choices.text: Keep softening them, and keep it secret

effects.log: You keep softening. At the year's end the two houses meet at a funeral and each thanks the other for the courtesy of their letters, and you stay silent.

choices.text: Tell both houses what you have done

effects.log: You tell them. They are cross, and then mortified, and then, to your enormous relief, laughing.

events.text: The head of {b3_house} asks you, during your year, to witness a will. The will leaves the house's oldest property to a person nobody has heard of. The witnesses are three: the steward, the cook, and you. The head signs with a hand that shakes slightly, and looks at none of you.

choices.text: Witness it, and keep the name to yourself

effects.log: You witness it, and keep the name. Years later you learn the person was a child the head had once wronged, and you are glad of your silence.

choices.text: Witness it, and quietly find the person

effects.log: You find the person, a grown stranger, and tell them. It is a very odd, very tender meeting, and the house is, later, grateful, in its way.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} has a dozen old lamps that must never go out, and a family of lamp-keepers who have kept them for nine hundred years. This year the last keeper is dying. You are asked to learn the craft. It is a very small, very exacting art, and a very lonely one.

choices.text: Learn it, and take the post for the year

effects.log: You learn it. It takes a year of nights, and you keep the lamps lit, and the last keeper dies content, and the house is quietly, forever, in your debt.

choices.text: Find and train a young keeper instead

effects.log: You find and train a young keeper. The craft survives, and you are the sponsor of a thing the house had thought lost.

events.text: You spend your year in {b3_house} as the cook's helper, a post the house gave you with a perfectly straight face. It is real work: the peeling, the stirring, the carrying. The cook is a tyrant and a poet. By the end you are the only person who has ever been told that a sauce is not bad.

choices.text: Take the post gladly, and learn everything

effects.log: You take it gladly. By spring you can cook the house's whole feast of the founders, and the cook, quietly, gives you a worn knife.

choices.text: Do it, and say it is beneath you, mildly

effects.log: You say so, mildly. The cook roars, and then laughs, and the house, hearing, makes you the object of a long, affectionate joke.

events.text: It is a year of rain, and {b3_house} has gone damp in every corner. The head asks you to see to the great drain. Nobody else will. There are things in the drain, old things, a boot, a ring, a very old crest. The steward watches, from a dry place, with interest.

choices.text: Clear the drain yourself, and keep the finds for the house

effects.log: You clear it. The crest is of an older branch, long thought lost, and the house puts it in the Cloud Tablet hall with a small ceremony.

choices.text: Hire labourers and oversee from the dry

effects.log: You hire labourers and oversee. It is done well and quickly, and the steward notes you did not get your own hands dirty.

events.text: You are the house's guest-keeper for a year, and discover that the greatest skill in {b3_house} is to make a visitor feel that they are the only one who matters, while keeping three others in the next room. The art is knowing exactly which door to open, and when.

choices.text: Master it, with the steward's coaching

effects.log: You master it. The steward is proud, and you are, by the end, the most sought-after host in the district, and the head says it has been a wise appointment.

choices.text: Be plain with every guest instead

effects.log: You are plain with them. It is a sensation, and a few are shocked, and a few return, years later, simply to be spoken to honestly.

events.text: You sit, for the first time, in the head's seat of {b3_house}. It is a hard seat, deliberately; the founder thought comfort led to error. Down the table, a very old uncle of the blood has not touched his food. He is looking at you the way one looks at a stain. Nobody has spoken for a very long minute.

choices.text: Say a few plain words, and offer wine

effects.log: You say a few plain words and offer the wine. It is poured, and drunk, by most, and the uncle sets down his cup, untouched, and goes on staring.

choices.text: Say nothing; let the silence be your first act

effects.log: You say nothing. It is a long silence, and after a while the oldest voice, the uncle's, breaks it with a cough, and the meal begins.

events.text: The blood of {b3_house} do not bow to you in the hall. They stand, correctly, and fold their hands, and tilt their heads exactly one finger. It is perfect, and an insult, and every child in the house will remember being taught it. The steward, at your side, says the blood needs time.

choices.text: Return the tilt, to each, exactly

effects.log: You return each tilt exactly. It is a long ceremony, and by the third row a few of them are fighting a smile, and it is a start.

choices.text: Bow to each, deeply, as a guest of the house

effects.log: You bow deeply to each. They are discomposed, and it is awful, and also, in a strange way, a kind of conquest.

events.text: The ancestral records of {b3_house} are brought, with ceremony, and you are asked to sign your name beneath the heads of the line. The ink is old, the page is old, and the space under the last name is, by long habit, left wide. You have never signed anything with such weight.

choices.text: Sign in your own plain hand

effects.log: You sign in your own hand, plainly. The blood murmur at its lack of flourish, and the oldest of them, later, says it is the most honest signature in the book.

choices.text: Sign in the old style, as the heads did

effects.log: You sign in the old style. It is a flawless imitation, and the blood approve, and you feel, as you write, a little like a forger.

events.text: A sealed letter was left for the next head of {b3_house} by the last, who did not expect it to be you. It is read to you by the steward in a flat voice. It says that the new head is a thief and an outsider, and that the house will survive them. The steward, without comment, folds it.

choices.text: Ask that the letter be kept in the archive, unaltered

effects.log: You have it kept, unaltered. The house is shaken that you did not burn it, and it is, to some, the first good sign.

choices.text: Write a reply, and have it filed beside

effects.log: You write a reply, three lines, and have it filed beside. In a hundred years, someone will read both, and laugh.

events.text: On your first night as head of {b3_house}, you find the door of the study ajar, and a very young cousin sitting at the desk in the dark, trying on the seal. The child freezes, enormous-eyed. It is the best, bravest, worst-timed thing, and the whole house will say the head must punish it.

choices.text: Let the child try it, and say nothing

effects.log: You let the child hold the seal for a minute, and say nothing. The child is, from then on, devoted to you, and the secret becomes the best kind of bond.

choices.text: Return the seal to its box, kindly, and send the child to bed

effects.log: You do so. It is gentle and correct, and the child never tries it again, and is, much later, a fine head of its own.

events.text: The old head of {b3_house}, whom you displaced, sits in the front row at your first assembly. They are impeccable. They are completely still. At the end of your address, they stand, and walk to you, and take your hand, and say, loud enough for all, that the house is in good hands. They are the best liar you have ever met.

choices.text: Thank them, and ask for their counsel

effects.log: You thank them, and ask. They are caught between rage and pride, and agree, and are, for a year, a brilliant, grudging adviser, and then, strangely, a friend.

choices.text: Thank them, and ask nothing of them

effects.log: You thank them, and ask nothing. They retire to the east wing and are never seen again, except at funerals.

events.text: The blood of {b3_house} want a feast to mark your accession, and they want to pay for it from your private means. It is a test, and a tax, and a very old custom. The steward, beside you, whispers the sum, and it is large, and it must be answered in a moment, aloud, before witnesses.

choices.text: Agree gladly, and ask them to choose the menu

effects.log: You agree and let them choose. They spend the evening happier than they had meant to, and the sum, in the end, was less than feared.

choices.text: Say the house pays from the common store, as it always has

effects.log: You say so. The blood are a little scandalised that you know the custom, and a little pleased, and the feast is smaller.

events.text: The wives, husbands and widows of {b3_house}, a body of old women and a few resigned men, come to you in a body, to ask what you intend for them. It is not a petition. It is an inspection. They are the real memory of the house, and the true bench of judges, and they are not smiling.

choices.text: Promise them their rooms and their say

effects.log: You promise it, and keep it. They are, to a person, pleased, and say nothing, and in a year they are the best allies you have.

choices.text: Say you will see each of them alone, and ask what they need

effects.log: You see each of them alone. It takes a month, and it is the best month of the year, and you learn the house.

events.text: You discover, on your first day as head of {b3_house}, that the house has no enemies listed. It has grudges, of course, but they are kept in the memory of the aunts and not in the books. When you ask the steward to write them down, the steward goes pale and says that to write a grudge is to make it eternal.

choices.text: Let them stay unwritten

effects.log: You let them stay unwritten. The aunts nod, and the house keeps its old, living, fading grudges, and does not make new ones.

choices.text: Have them written, quietly, for your eyes only

effects.log: You have them written, and read them in a night. You wish you had not, and you know the house, now, to its roots.

events.text: An envoy of a rival house comes to you in {b3_house} on the very day you take the seat, carrying a congratulation so elegantly worded that you cannot tell which part is the knife. The envoy smiles. The blood watch. A servant, silently, refills every cup but yours.

choices.text: Answer in kind, with a gift that has no edge

effects.log: You answer with a plain, good gift. The envoy is, for a moment, unsure how to take it, and the blood are delighted.

choices.text: Ask the envoy to read the congratulation aloud again, slowly

effects.log: You ask. The envoy, caught, reads it again, and by the third line the room is smiling, and the envoy is less sure of the knife.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} has a tradition that a new head must go, alone, at dawn, to the grave of the founder, and say aloud what they intend. Nobody has heard what is said. A very small bell is rung on return. You go up the path in grey light, and the whole house is awake, and not looking.

choices.text: Say what you truly intend, aloud, to the stone

effects.log: You say it, aloud, plainly. The wind is the only listener, and when you come down the bell is rung by a child, and the house, for no reason it can name, is quieter.

choices.text: Sit in silence, and leave

effects.log: You sit in silence. You come down, and the bell is rung, and the house thinks you have said something terrible, and is awed.

events.text: The blood of {b3_house} have prepared, as a courtesy, a list of what they expect the new head to change, and of what they expect the new head to leave alone. The lists are the same length. They are in alphabetical order. They are signed by every adult of the house, and at the bottom, in small letters, a joke.

choices.text: Read the lists aloud, and the joke

effects.log: You read them aloud, with the joke. The room breaks, a little, and the lists are, from that day, a thing of fondness.

choices.text: Keep the lists, and promise nothing

effects.log: You keep the lists, and promise nothing, and the house knows precisely where it stands.

events.text: A cousin of the blood of {b3_house} mocks you, in the hall, in front of the young, by repeating your own words in an exact, slow, cruel imitation. It is skilled. It is awful. The young are watching you, and the cousin knows it, and the aunts have all stopped chewing.

choices.text: Laugh, and ask for the imitation again

effects.log: You laugh, and ask for it again. The cousin, thrown, does it a second time, and it is worse, and the hall laughs with you, and the cousin goes red.

choices.text: Rise, and answer in the cousin's own voice

effects.log: You answer in the cousin's voice, exactly. The hall is stunned, and the cousin bows low, and it is a fine, cruel, honest bout.

events.text: You have ruled {b3_house} for some years, and the blood still call you "the head" in a tone that means "for now". It is not hostility. It is an old, steady, unmoving patience. They will outlast you, they believe, and the believing is the strength of the house.

choices.text: Plan for a long head's rule, and begin a work that takes a century

effects.log: You begin it: a library, a canal, a school. The blood resent it, and in a hundred years it will be the house's pride.

choices.text: Accept the tone, and rule lightly

effects.log: You accept it. The house is easy, and the blood amused, and a long, mild peace settles.

events.text: A matter comes before you as head of {b3_house} that the whole house expects you to decide against the outsider you once were. A distant relative of the blood, a hard case, has come asking for the same chance you took. The blood are watching.

choices.text: Give the relative a place, as you were given one

effects.log: You give a place. The blood grumble and the relative is, in a decade, the house's best steward, and a living argument.

choices.text: Rule against, citing the house's custom

effects.log: You rule against. It is lawful, and it is a betrayal of yourself, and the blood approve, and you do not.

events.text: The feast of {b3_house} comes round, and the blood seat you where the head sits. But the first dish passes you, and goes to an old uncle, as it did under the old head, and nobody has told you. The table waits, with great interest, for whether you notice.

choices.text: Let the uncle have the first dish, and take the second

effects.log: You let him have it. The uncle, flustered, tries to give it back, and it is a lovely, awkward moment, and the house loves you for it.

choices.text: Take the first dish, and say why

effects.log: You take it, and say, mildly, that the head takes first, and the house is a little silent, and then, to your relief, the old uncle nods.

events.text: A young one of the blood of {b3_house}, a rising star, asks for leave to marry outside the families, to someone the house calls beneath it. It is not forbidden. It is simply never done. The aunts have already gathered. The young one stands in the study, looking as if about to be sick.

choices.text: Grant leave, and attend the wedding

effects.log: You grant it, and attend. The aunts are scandalised, and then charmed by the bride, and in a year it is a family legend.

choices.text: Delay for a year, and see

effects.log: You delay. The young one, in a year, is no less sure, and the house, in the end, bends, and the delay is remembered as a small cruelty.

events.text: The portrait of every head of {b3_house} hangs in the great hall, and it is the custom that on the day of your tenth year yours is added. The painter has been in the house for a month. The painter has asked you to smile, and you cannot, and the blood have gathered to watch.

choices.text: Sit as you are, unsmiling, for the whole sitting

effects.log: You sit, unsmiling. The portrait is stern, accurate and, later generations say, the best of the gallery.

choices.text: Tell the painter a bad story, and be painted laughing

effects.log: You tell it. The painter is a genius, and you are painted laughing, and it is hung at the end, and the blood wince, and the young adore it.

events.text: A scandal in {b3_house}: a branch has been selling, quietly, the house name to merchants who print it on their goods. It is dreadful, and a little ingenious. The blood want the branch struck from the register. The branch's elder, a woman of sixty, arrives at your door and sits down, and says she would like to explain.

choices.text: Hear her out, and fine the branch, with a licence

effects.log: You hear her, and fine the branch, and license the trade. It is cleverer than either side expected, and the house is richer by the year.

choices.text: Strike the branch from the register

effects.log: You strike it. It is just, and cold, and the branch's elder bows, and the blood approve, and the house is a little smaller and a little prouder.

events.text: Among the blood of {b3_house}, an old argument surfaces, of which of two founding stories is true. Neither is. The head is the only one who has read the oldest papers, and now the blood want you to rule. It is a rare chance to tell a house a truth it has never been ready for.

choices.text: Tell them the truth, plainly, and in public

effects.log: You tell them. It is a stunned silence, and a mild scandal, and by next year the house, to its surprise, prefers it.

choices.text: Rule that both stories are true, and keep the papers

effects.log: You rule so. The house is content, and the papers are put in a box, and the box is put in a cellar, and you sleep slightly worse.

events.text: You have been long, now, at the head of {b3_house}, by the reckoning of the blood. They have started asking, politely, who you will name. The names come in whispers, by the aunts, by the cousins, by a very serious child. It is the question of the age, and it is not yet time to answer.

choices.text: Name no one, and say the house will know

effects.log: You name no one. The house argues for a decade, and it is, in the end, the best argument the house has had, and it chooses well.

choices.text: Name someone, and say it aloud

effects.log: You name someone. The house is divided, and the one named is terrified, and it is done, and the blood are almost relieved.

events.text: The house of {b3_house} sends you, as its head, an invitation to its own annual reckoning, a thing the head has always attended and which no head has ever enjoyed. Each branch gives an account of the year, in order, in public. The accounts are honest, bruising, and long. They are, by the end, very moving.

choices.text: Attend, and answer every branch in turn

effects.log: You answer each. It takes three days, and you leave hoarse and exhausted, and the house is, for years, a better house.

choices.text: Attend the first day, and send a deputy

effects.log: You send a deputy. It is practical, and noted, and the house is a little cooler about it, and no harm done.

events.text: A famine strikes the lands that pay tribute to {b3_house}. The tribute is, by ancient right, due. The blood say it must be taken, or the house will be thought weak. The tenants, in their hundreds, come to the gate in silence, and stand there, and do not ask for anything.

choices.text: Waive the tribute, and open the stores

effects.log: You waive it, and open them. The blood are aghast, and the tenants are, for a century, the most loyal in the district.

choices.text: Halve it, and say it is a loan

effects.log: You halve it. It is a compromise, and the blood grumble, and the tenants nod, and the house is neither loved nor hated.

events.text: Years in, the blood of {b3_house} have a name for you in private: the Lodger. It is said fondly, now, and with a kind of pride. You hear it, one day, from a child in the corridor, who does not know you are listening. The child says it as if it were a title of honour.

choices.text: Take the name, and sign with it once

effects.log: You sign a letter with it. The blood hear, and are quietly moved, and the name is carved on a beam of the hall.

choices.text: Pretend you did not hear it

effects.log: You pretend. It is kinder to everyone, and you are, for the rest of your tenure, the Lodger, and glad.

events.text: A very old aunt of {b3_house}, on her deathbed, asks for the head. When you come, she takes your hand, and says she was wrong about you, and that she is sorry, and that she would like to be buried by the door. It is a small, weak, firm voice. The whole house is in the corridor.

choices.text: Promise it, and keep the promise

effects.log: You promise. She dies at dusk, and is buried by the door, and the whole house comes to the grave, and the blood, for the first time, call you by your name.

choices.text: Say there is nothing to forgive

effects.log: You say so. She smiles, and is gone before morning, and the corridor is quiet, and a tablet is added.

events.text: Two of the blood of {b3_house} have each come to you in secret, each to ask you to cut off the other from the inheritance. They are twins, and bitter, and nobody knows how it began. The two petitions are in your hands, in the same handwriting, with the same turns of phrase.

choices.text: Show each the other's petition

effects.log: You show them. They are speechless, and then, slowly, reconciled, in a way that is awkward and permanent.

choices.text: Grant neither, and say it is a house matter

effects.log: You grant neither. They resent you jointly, which is, for twins, a bond.

events.text: The porter of {b3_house} takes your card, reads it, turns it over to read the back, which is blank, and asks whether you have an appointment. You do not. The porter nods as if you had named a crime, and says the house will "consider" it. You are shown to a bench in the gatehouse. It has been polished by the waiting of centuries.

choices.text: Wait on the bench until you are seen

effects.log: You wait. It takes three hours. The porter, passing, drops one remark about the tea, and you are suddenly shown through.

choices.text: Leave a note praising the bench and depart

effects.log: You leave the note. It is read aloud in the house at supper and considered both insolent and, to a few, charming.

events.text: In the hall of {b3_house}, the long table is laid for forty, and you are placed at the thirty-eighth seat, between a very old man who has fallen asleep and a child who is staring. The talk is of matters you can barely follow. The child leans over and whispers that nobody at the table likes the soup.

choices.text: Whisper back that you do not either

effects.log: The child nearly spills the soup with delight, and you have, in the child, an ally that will matter in the house for a hundred years.

choices.text: Eat the soup in silence, with every sign of enjoyment

effects.log: You eat it to the bottom. The old man wakes, observes this, and says it is the first time a guest has done so.

events.text: Your task for {b3_house} is to carry a sealed box to another house, unopened. It is light. It rattles slightly. The messenger who gave it to you has gone pale. Halfway there, in a quiet lane, the box begins to hum.

choices.text: Carry it on, humming, and deliver it

effects.log: You deliver it. The receiving house opens it before you, and finds a single feather, which makes them go silent. You are paid in a favour no one explains.

choices.text: Open the box in the lane

effects.log: You open it. A moth the colour of dusk rises and goes away over the roofs. The house, informed, is annoyed and slightly impressed.

events.text: The house has asked you to copy the record of a debt: a hundred and four lines of names in a very small hand. About line forty, you notice that one name is repeated, with a different amount, in a different ink. The copyist before you knew. They left it as it was. You have a brush and a choice.

choices.text: Copy it exactly, discrepancy and all

effects.log: You copy it exactly. The head of the house reads your copy and says only that you are the first copyist in a century to have eyes.

choices.text: Quietly correct the figure to match the first

effects.log: You correct it. It is the neater page, and the house is pleased, and you carry a faint weight of having decided.

events.text: A junior cousin of {b3_house} has been put under your charge for an errand to the capital. The cousin is cheerful, incompetent, and beloved. On the road, a bridge is out. The cousin proposes, with great confidence, a ford that you can see is deep.

choices.text: Overrule the cousin and take the long way

effects.log: You take the long way. The cousin sulks for a day, then spots a rare bird, and forgets everything. You arrive late, but arrive.

choices.text: Try the ford, with a rope

effects.log: You try it with a rope. The cousin is swept off, hauled back, gleeful, and wants to do it again. The house hears of it and is torn between fury and delight.

events.text: The chief steward of {b3_house} sets you to organise the great ledger of the years. It is a heap, in no order, in nine hands, over a thousand years. At the bottom of the heap is a thin book, much-thumbed, titled "What Is Owed to Us." You have not been told to read it.

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: You read it. It is a list of every kindness the house has received and not yet repaid. The steward, finding you at it, says you are the first to have wept at the third page.

choices.text: Put it back unread and finish the ledger

effects.log: You put it back. The ledger is done in a season, in perfect order, and the steward thanks you, and hands you the thin book with a bow.

events.text: In the service of {b3_house} you are asked to meet a visiting official at the gate and see that nothing goes wrong. The official is very short, very polite, and a person of rank so high that the house refuses to say it aloud. The official asks, kindly, to be shown the kitchens.

choices.text: Show the official the kitchens, as asked

effects.log: You show them. The official tastes six things, says nothing, and leaves a gift on the table. The cook cries for an hour.

choices.text: Politely propose the library instead

effects.log: You propose the library. The official is delighted, and spends three hours in it, and the house is quietly relieved, and the cook is insulted.

events.text: The household of {b3_house} has lost a prized cat. You are sent to find it. The cat is found in under an hour, asleep in the head's own bed. The head, enraged by the intrusion, but unable to say so, is already pale with fondness. They ask you, in strictest confidence, to tell the household the cat is still missing.

choices.text: Tell the household the cat is still missing

effects.log: You tell them. For a week the whole house searches, and the head sleeps with a cat, and is calmer than at any point in years.

choices.text: Say the cat is found, and in the right bed

effects.log: You say so. The household laughs, and the head turns the colour of persimmon, and the cat is removed to a cushion by the door, where it resumes sleeping.

events.text: You are loaned to a distant branch of {b3_house} to teach their children manners. The children are not unruly; they are formal, small and terrifying. They greet you in unison, tilt exactly one finger, and say "we have been taught by better." You have a lesson plan. They have a delegation.

choices.text: Teach them to be badly behaved, a little, on purpose

effects.log: You teach them to laugh. By the end of the month the delegation is in the orchard, up a tree, and their parents are in tears and grateful.

choices.text: Teach them the manners of a different house, entirely

effects.log: You teach them another house's manners, and the children, meticulous, adopt them in a day, and the parents are appalled.

events.text: A decade into your tenure as head of {b3_house}, a letter from the neighbouring house proposes a joint festival. The two houses have never shared anything. Your council is divided: some for friendship, some for the principle that principle is all they have. The festival would require the opening of the old gate.

choices.text: Open the old gate, and share the festival

effects.log: You open it. The festival is stiff, and then not, and by the end the gate has a new hinge, and the two houses a shared joke.

choices.text: Refuse, and propose a smaller gathering at the border

effects.log: You propose a gathering at the border. It is held in a field, with a rope between, and the first agreement is that the rope may be dropped.

events.text: The blood of {b3_house} have asked you to settle the question of the third bell: whether it rings at dusk, or a little after. Some say dusk; some say after; both sides have text. You find that nobody now alive knows why it matters. All of them are certain it does.

choices.text: Ring it at dusk, and let the argument stand

effects.log: You ring it at dusk. The "after" faction is outraged, and the matter is regarded as settled and unfinished, which is what the house prefers.

choices.text: Ring it at the exact moment of the sun's edge, and measure

effects.log: You ring it at the edge. A scholar measures. The bell falls a minute after dusk, and the factions are, to their own astonishment, both vindicated.

events.text: A young member of {b3_house} comes before you in the hall and confesses to a small crime: they have been secretly giving the house's medicine to the poor of the lower town. Your steward demands a punishment. The house's law has one, and it is harsh. The young person stands very straight.

choices.text: Reduce the penalty to a lecture and a share of the work

effects.log: You reduce it. The young one becomes the house's almoner, and the lower town hangs a lantern for them.

choices.text: Apply the law, but pay the cost yourself

effects.log: You pay it. The house gasps at the cost, and the young one understands, with a start, what it means to lead.

events.text: The treasury of {b3_house} has a surplus for the first time in your tenure. The blood want a feast, a monument, a renovation, a trip. The steward wants to save it. A child, overhearing, says the house should buy a very large cat.

choices.text: Spend a third on a feast, a third on repair, and a third on a very large cat

effects.log: You do. The cat is magnificent, the feast is merry, the roof holds, and the house will tell the story for a hundred years.

choices.text: Save it all, and put the sum into the school

effects.log: You put it in the school. In twenty years the school is the best in the district, and the house has no cat.

events.text: The oldest servant of {b3_house} asks to speak to the head alone. In the study, hands trembling, the servant says that the household's heirloom, the great seal, is not the original. The original was lost a century ago, and replaced in secret, and the servant has known all along. The servant is dying and cannot carry it further.

choices.text: Absolve the servant, and keep the secret

effects.log: You absolve. The servant weeps and thanks you, and dies the next week, lighter. The seal, since then, has been quietly the real one.

choices.text: Announce the truth to the house

effects.log: You announce it. The house reels, and then, remarkably, nothing changes, because the seal was always the house's decision, and not a thing.

events.text: Three branches of {b3_house} present three plans for the same field. Each is excellent. Each excludes the other two. They will not compromise. The field has lain fallow for seven years while they argue. A tenant, standing by, politely suggests the field would like to be planted.

choices.text: Plant it with something none of the three proposed

effects.log: You plant it with a crop none suggested. The harvest is middling, and the three branches, outflanked, share the cost of complaining.

choices.text: Divide the field in three, and let them see

effects.log: You divide it. Within two seasons the three are visiting each other's plots, stealing ideas, and the field is a patchwork of rivalry and thrift.

events.text: A famous monk is passing through the territory of {b3_house} and requests to speak with the head. The monk sits across from you for an hour in silence and finally says: "I came to see whether you were worth the trouble people say you cause." The monk waits. The tea cools.

choices.text: Ask what trouble people say

effects.log: The monk, to your surprise, laughs. He lists eleven. Nine are true. You thank him, and he says that is the tenth.

choices.text: Answer: "enough to be getting on with"

effects.log: The monk bows, rises, and walks out without a word, and you hear him laughing in the courtyard all the way to the gate.

events.text: The eldest aunt of {b3_house} comes to demand that the household return to the practice of wearing the old robes at dinner. She is frail and fierce. The younger generation hates the old robes, which are heavy and stiff and smell of camphor. She says she will be dead soon and that it is a small thing to ask.

choices.text: Agree to the robes for one dinner a month

effects.log: You agree. The robes are worn once a month, and the dinner is the most memorable of the month, and the aunt is seated at the head, as she wished, in her glory.

choices.text: Hold a vote of the whole household

effects.log: You hold it. The robes win by one vote, which is the aunt's, and the house obeys cheerfully, because she is not wrong about anything but the camphor.

events.text: A historian arrives to write a life of the last head of {b3_house}, your predecessor, and asks to interview you. The historian is quite plainly in love with the predecessor. The first question is "How did you feel about being the successor of the greatest head the house has had?" The room is warm. You are expected to say something modest.

choices.text: Say you never expected to measure up, and have not tried

effects.log: You say so. The historian, startled, writes it down, and a section of the book is rewritten around a head who had no wish to be a legend.

choices.text: Say the predecessor was greatest at being forgiven

effects.log: You say so. The historian looks up, wide-eyed, and the book is a finer one for it.

events.text: The isle bell at {b3_house} is struck by an unseasonal wind, and every roof tile on the east side lifts and falls in a perfect wave. No one is hurt. The tiles are in order, but slightly rotated. The steward counts them and reports that every tile has been rotated exactly a degree, in the same direction.

choices.text: Leave the tiles as they are

effects.log: You leave them. The roof, thereafter, sheds rain better, and sheds it into the cistern, which has never been so full.

choices.text: Have the tiles turned back, and note the date

effects.log: You turn them back and note it. Next year the wind comes again, and the tiles turn again, and you give up and let the roof have its way.

events.text: A pair of clerks of {b3_house} have been feuding over the use of a single inkwell. They glare at each other across the clerks' room. The inkwell is the only one with good ink. A third clerk has quietly bought a new inkwell, and kept it a secret, and is making quite a bit of money by letting the others use it.

choices.text: Confront the third clerk gently, and ask them to share

effects.log: You do. The third clerk is mortified, and gives the inkwell to the room, and the feud dissolves in the shame of the whole.

choices.text: Buy a fourth inkwell, and a fifth, and a sixth

effects.log: You buy six. The clerks, awash in ink, can find nothing more to quarrel about, and begin a new feud about which is the best.

events.text: Your steward reports that the walls of {b3_house} have begun to emit a faint, constant smell of plum. It is not unpleasant. It is simply everywhere. Guests remark on it. The house has never been so beloved. The steward is suspicious, and proposes to have the walls inspected.

choices.text: Leave the plum alone, and enjoy it

effects.log: You enjoy it. For a decade the house smells of plum, and then, one spring, of something else, and you regret it, quietly, and for years.

choices.text: Inspect the walls

effects.log: You inspect. Behind a panel is a small tin of preserved plums, left by a builder five hundred years ago, long sealed, perfectly good. The house has a feast.

events.text: A rule of {b3_house} states that on the anniversary of the founder's death, no one may speak between dusk and dawn. This year the anniversary falls on the night of a visiting dignitary's arrival. The dignitary speaks. The house cannot answer. The dignitary, puzzled, speaks again. The silence is excruciating.

choices.text: Break the silence yourself, with a bow

effects.log: You bow, and speak. The house is aghast, and then, seeing the dignitary's relief, relieved. The founder, you reflect, would have done the same.

choices.text: Answer with elaborate gestures, in perfect silence

effects.log: You answer in gesture. The dignitary, enchanted, replies in kind, and the house watches the best silent conversation of its history.

events.text: The treasurer of {b3_house} announces that, by long tradition, each head must on taking office leave a gift to the house. You have been in office twenty years without doing so. The treasurer says that it is overdue, apologetically, and that the usual gift is a tree.

choices.text: Plant a tree, and a small plaque with an honest sentence

effects.log: You plant it. The plaque reads "Late." The house loves it, and the tree, of all the heads' trees, is the best-watered.

choices.text: Give the house something else: a school hall

effects.log: You give the hall. It is not a tree. The treasurer is silent a long moment, and records it as "a tree, in a certain sense."

events.text: The house of {b3_house} is asked to host the yearly assembly of the great houses, a ruinously expensive honour that comes round every forty years. It is the turn of {b3_house}. The treasurer is in despair. The guest list is long, and contains six pairs of mortal enemies and one pair of recent newlyweds.

choices.text: Accept, and seat the enemies by lot

effects.log: You accept and seat them by lot. The luck is unbelievable: three enemy pairs draw adjacent seats, and the feast is a series of small miracles of courtesy.

choices.text: Accept, and seat the newlyweds with the enemies

effects.log: You seat them as buffers. The newlyweds are so radiantly happy that the enemies forget their grudges for the length of a dinner, which is as long as one needs.

events.text: A dispute at the gate of {b3_house}: two carters, each with a cart of grain, each claiming the right of way through the narrow arch. Neither will yield. The traffic behind them is half a mile long. A passing child suggests the head decide. The child is, as it happens, the head's own.

choices.text: Have both carts unload, pass the grain through by hand, and reload

effects.log: You do it. It takes three hours and a hundred hands, and by the end the carters are friends, and have invented a pulley.

choices.text: Ask the child which cart should go first

effects.log: The child says the one with the smaller wheel. It is correct. You never learn why, and the child never says.

events.text: {npc} asks to be shown the oldest thing in your house. You hesitate, then take {him} to the cellar, where a plain clay jar is kept on a shelf, nameless, sealed with wax. {npc} puts a hand on it for a long moment and says, "it is warm." It is not. But {his} hand, when withdrawn, leaves a faint mark on the dust.

choices.text: Say the jar has been warm as long as you can remember

effects.log: You say so. It is true, you realise, as you say it. {npc} looks at you with something like awe, and the match, from there, is not an arrangement.

choices.text: Say nothing, and take {his} hand off the jar

effects.log: You lead {him} out. {npc} says nothing, but later that evening, at supper, reaches for your hand without looking.

events.text: A year into your headship of {b3_house}, the blood begin to send you their problems in the form of small written petitions, tied in red thread, left on your desk at night. You find eleven this morning. The topics range from the quality of the soup to whether a cousin may marry a gardener. {b3_house} has not been so honest in a century.

choices.text: Answer every petition in your own hand

effects.log: You answer all eleven. By the end of the month the thread has become a custom, and the house runs a little more gently on the paper.

choices.text: Set aside one evening a week for petitions, and read them aloud

effects.log: You set the evening. The house assembles, and it is a theatre of embarrassed smiles and small justice.

events.text: An old rival of {b3_house} sends congratulations on your headship, along with a gift: a handsome knife. The note says it is "for opening letters." The gift is exquisite and slightly menacing. The household watches the box.

choices.text: Use the knife for letters, publicly

effects.log: You use it. The rival, hearing, is both gratified and slightly alarmed, and the house gains a reputation for fearlessness.

choices.text: Return the knife with a handsome inkstone

effects.log: You return it. The rival is silent for a season, and then sends a second, kinder gift.

events.text: The treasury of {b3_house}, under your hand, has grown a little, and the blood are restless. A cousin suggests a monument to your headship. You are mortified. A second cousin suggests a monument to the founder. You are relieved. A third suggests a monument to the cat. The house is unanimous.

choices.text: Build the monument to the cat

effects.log: You build it. It is the finest in the district, and the cat, an ancient grey tom, is painted in his element and accepts the honour with hauteur.

choices.text: Build nothing, and spend the sum on the lower town's wells

effects.log: You dig wells. The lower town names a well for you, and you let them.

events.text: At the head's table of {b3_house}, a seat that has stood empty since before you came is quietly kept. A servant sets a bowl before it each night. When you ask about it, the oldest says it is for "the one who comes when the house is at its worst." No one has sat there in four hundred years.

choices.text: Have the bowl left in place

effects.log: You leave it. One night, near dawn, the bowl is empty, and clean, and the servants swear they did not touch it.

choices.text: Sit in the seat yourself, for one meal

effects.log: You sit. The house holds its breath. The meal passes without incident, and the seat seems, at its end, very slightly warmer.

events.text: A messenger from a distant house arrives with a request that {b3_house} take in, for three years, a boy of ten, the heir of a house in ruins. The boy is solemn and polite and carries his whole life in a single bag. The blood mutter that the house has enough mouths. You find the boy staring at the fish in the pond.

choices.text: Take the boy in as one of the house

effects.log: You take him. In three years he leaves, tall, and a gentle man, and the ruined house rises, in time, with {b3_house} as its first and only friend.

choices.text: Place the boy with a tutor of the house and watch from a distance

effects.log: You place him. He thrives, quietly, and writes you a letter each new year, a single line, always about the fish.

events.text: The cave is cold and swept. {b3_anc} sits at the back of it with eyes shut and one hand open on a knee, and on the open hand a spider has spun a small, careful web. Nothing about the sleeper has aged, and nothing has moved. On the floor, a bowl of rice from this morning.

choices.text: Sit down across from {b3_anc} and wait

effects.log: You sit down and wait. Nothing happens for hours, and then the web trembles once, as at a breath, and you go home sure you were seen.

choices.text: Leave an offering and go quietly

effects.log: You leave a small offering and go quietly. Somebody will sweep it away by dawn, and you have the odd feeling of having been polite in the right language.

events.text: A maid is on her knees in the cave mouth of {b3_anc} with a broom, sweeping a floor that is already clean. She says the house has paid for this sweeping every morning since before the house had a name. She asks you, not unkindly, not to disturb the dust on the sleeper's side.

choices.text: Take a second broom and help her

effects.log: You help her sweep until the light turns. She tells you three things about the house that are not in the ledger, and all three turn out true.

choices.text: Ask how long she has done it

effects.log: She has done it forty years, and her mother did it before, and she has never once seen the sleeper's eyes open. She says it as one speaks of the weather.

events.text: Carved into the wall beside {b3_anc} are tally marks, in rows, each row a century, each row ending in the same small sign. Somebody has counted every year of the sleep, and kept counting past the point where it made any sense. The last row is fresh.

choices.text: Add your own mark to the last row

effects.log: You scratch one mark. It feels a little like signing a witness book at a bed that is not yet a grave, and it is somehow the right amount of respect.

choices.text: Read the rows and keep what they say to yourself

effects.log: You read them all by candle. The count and the house's own chronicle disagree by eleven years, and you tell nobody, since the disagreement is the only interesting thing about the place.

events.text: It is not what the house told you. {b3_anc} is awake, and sits with open eyes, and does not speak. They look at you for as long as it takes a candle to burn a finger down, and then at the cave wall, as if the matter of you has been judged and put aside for later.

choices.text: Bow and withdraw backward

effects.log: You bow, and withdraw backward the whole length of the cave, and nothing follows you. The house, when you tell them, goes quiet and then sends wine.

choices.text: Speak your name and your errand plainly

effects.log: You say your name and your errand. The eyes close in the middle of the word errand, and you are never sure whether you were answered or dismissed.

events.text: On the hillside below {b3_anc}'s cave there is a small child's grave, tended, with fresh markers. The steward says it belonged to the ancestor's own, long before anyone now living. The sleeper keeps the grave in their sleep, in a way the house has never understood.

choices.text: Lay something on the grave

effects.log: You lay a small thing on it. The next morning there is a single leaf set upon it in return, in a pattern, and it is the nearest thing to a letter you have ever had from the dead.

choices.text: Ask the steward to say nothing of it

effects.log: The steward agrees, with visible relief. It is the secret of the house, and you are now a keeper of it.

events.text: The house has a custom: any who climb to {b3_anc} must bring a question, and leave without an answer. You bring one. It is not a good one; you thought of it on the path. The cave is very still and it occurs to you that a better question would have cost you a better night.

choices.text: Ask it out loud anyway

effects.log: You ask it. Nothing answers, but a gust of wind passes through the cave and takes the candle, and you walk down in the dark feeling lighter than the question deserved.

choices.text: Keep the question, and make a better one by morning

effects.log: You keep it. You spend the night on the path making a better one, and by dawn you have a question that is about you, not about the house.

events.text: An old steward of the house, ancient and cross, finds you at the foot of {b3_anc}'s mountain. The steward says the sleeper is the house's one private debt: that the founders owe them something and nobody now knows what. They ask whether you intend to be one more person who tries to find out.

choices.text: Promise to ask nothing of the sleeper

effects.log: You promise it. The steward weeps without any change of expression and tells you the road is yours for as long as you keep your word.

choices.text: Say you will find out what the debt is

effects.log: You say so. The steward goes pale, then grim, and says to begin with the cellar of the third court, and not to take a lamp.

events.text: The sleeper {b3_anc} is not alone. At the edge of the cave sits a very old stone-clerk with a ledger, writing what the stillness does: the hours when the breath slows, when it quickens, when the room warms. It is the house's most guarded book. The clerk looks up at you, and then, pointedly, down.

choices.text: Ask to read a single page

effects.log: The clerk, to your amazement, allows it. You read the page, and learn that the sleeper's breath changed on the night you were born.

choices.text: Offer to sit a night as relief

effects.log: You take the clerk's stool for a night. It is the dullest and most solemn night of your life, and the clerk's gratitude is entire.

events.text: The cave has a second chamber that no one has opened. A crack of light shows under its door, the colour of dawn, regardless of the hour. The house forbids it. The door is not locked. {b3_anc}, sitting beside it, seems to be listening to it.

choices.text: Open the door a hand's breadth

effects.log: You open it a hand's breadth. There is nothing in it but a window onto a morning that is not today's, and a smell of rain. You close it, shaken.

choices.text: Obey the house and leave it shut

effects.log: You leave it shut. The light under it is still there as you walk down, and it follows you for a while like a small, hopeful dog.

events.text: Every year on one night the whole house climbs to {b3_anc} to be counted, as the old custom requires, so the sleeper knows who is still theirs. This year they count you, and the steward, reading, reaches your name and stops, and looks at the sleeper, and then says it aloud, a little louder than the rest.

choices.text: Answer "present", clearly

effects.log: You answer clearly. The crowd is silent, and then a very old woman says, so that all hear, that the house has not had an outsider answer that way in her time.

choices.text: Stand quietly and let the name be heard

effects.log: You stand quietly. It is heard, and it is written, and it is somehow more of a claim than a shout would have been.

events.text: A cousin of {b3_house} has climbed to {b3_anc} and returned changed. The cousin does not speak of it, and will not eat, and sits all day at the window. The house is divided about whether to be proud or afraid. They ask you to go up and see what the cousin saw.

choices.text: Go up, and sit where the cousin sat

effects.log: You sit there a day. You see the valley, nothing more, and then, for one moment at dusk, the valley as it will be in a thousand years, which you have never been able to describe.

choices.text: Tell the house to leave the cousin be

effects.log: You say so. The house accepts it, slowly. The cousin comes down on the seventh day, hungry and quite recovered, and grateful to you for the quiet.

events.text: In the cave of {b3_anc} a bell hangs, small and plain, on a cord of unwoven white. The house's rule is that it may be rung once in a life. A single note has never been struck in any living memory. It would be easy, and it would bring the house to its feet.

choices.text: Ring it once, softly

effects.log: You ring it softly. The note hangs a long time, and then, from far below, every bell in the house answers, and the house runs to the gate, and you take the blame with relish.

choices.text: Touch the cord and leave the bell silent

effects.log: You touch the cord and do not ring. The sleeper does not stir. In the evening the steward says the bell has been rung, once, by somebody, in the night, and does not look at you.

events.text: The ancestor's board among the cloud tablets is not where it should be; it has been turned to face the wall by someone long dead. The house never turns it back, for fear. You are the first to ask why. The steward says that when it faces the room, people stop being able to lie in it.

choices.text: Turn it to face the room, for one evening

effects.log: You turn it, and for an evening the house cannot tell a lie, and the dinner is the most honest and the most awful in its history. In the morning you turn it back, and some are fond.

choices.text: Leave it as it is

effects.log: You leave it. You know, now, why the house is so careful in speech, and you walk more softly in it afterward.

events.text: You have found out where {b3_anc} is, and you discover, with a pang, that you do not know what you want to do with the knowledge. The house watches you the way one watches a person holding a lit lamp in a granary. A very old servant says every finder of the cave has had the same face.

choices.text: Tell the house you will treat the cave with respect

effects.log: You say so. They accept it with the grace of a people who have been waiting centuries to be told it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and decide later

effects.log: You say nothing. The house, watching, files you with the cautious, and does not entirely mind.

events.text: The sleeper {b3_anc} is said to have fought a great war for the house. Carved above the cave mouth is a war-banner no one now can read. You copy it from memory and take it to the oldest scribe, who looks at it for a long time and says it is a lullaby.

choices.text: Ask the scribe to read the lullaby aloud

effects.log: The scribe reads it, flat, a verse at a time. The house falls into a hush, and the scribe stops at the fourth verse and cannot go on.

choices.text: Keep the lullaby for yourself

effects.log: You keep it. At night you find yourself humming it, and the tune, once learned, will not leave you, which seems to be the intention.

events.text: On the path up to {b3_anc} there are nine stones, and the house says each is a year of the sleeper's own youth. You count them going up and eight coming down. A boy of the house says the ninth has always been missing; that the sleeper keeps it in the cave, in their palm.

choices.text: Look for the ninth stone in the cave

effects.log: You look. The sleeper's hand is closed. Between the fingers there is a sliver of grey, and you do not touch it, and the place is stranger for the knowing.

choices.text: Place a stone of your own on the path

effects.log: You place one. By evening it is gone; by morning there is a tenth, nobody's, in its place, and the boy says he has never seen that either.

events.text: A traveller who calls at {b3_house} turns out to know of {b3_anc} by an older name. The traveller says that outside the house, far from here, the sleeper is a saint. There are shrines. The house has not been told. The traveller asks you whether the house would want to know.

choices.text: Take the traveller to the head of the house

effects.log: You take the traveller. The head hears the news in total silence and then thanks you, in a voice that is a little too even.

choices.text: Ask the traveller to keep it a secret for now

effects.log: The traveller agrees with a shrug. You hold a secret that is the exact weight of the house's whole pride, and learn to carry it lightly.

events.text: Late one evening you meet the house's old steward on the path up to {b3_anc}, carrying a flask. They say it is for the sleeper, as it has been for many years. The flask, they admit, is mostly for themselves. They ask, almost shyly, whether you would care for a drop.

choices.text: Share a cup with the steward on the stairs

effects.log: You share the cup. The steward tells you three truths about the house, all small, none flattering, and you carry them down in a kind of glad dread.

choices.text: Decline politely and walk the steward to the cave mouth

effects.log: You walk them to the cave mouth. They are touched, and sit, and for the first time in years someone watches them be quiet.

events.text: The sleeper's hair has grown, over the ages, and fills a corner of the cave, grey-white and fine as spun smoke. The house trims it once a year, with ceremony, and burns the trimmings. This year the steward asks you, as guest of honour, to cut the first lock. The shears are cold.

choices.text: Cut the lock, carefully

effects.log: You cut it. The shears sing, and the lock falls in a curl, and the steward catches it in a cloth and says you have steady hands, and means it as high praise.

choices.text: Decline, and hold the lamp instead
